title: The best Black Friday deals you can still get on AirPods, Macs, and other Apple gear
author: Brad Bourque, Sheena Vasani
text:
Black Friday is entering the evening, which means one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch is coming to a close. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts still apply to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro , too, which are available at their lowest prices to date.

In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers.

Earbud and headphone deals

You can buy the on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. Apple’s last-gen earbuds lack active noise cancellation, but they still deliver good, relatively bass-rich sound, even if they don’t quite match the newer AirPods 5. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review .

The are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon and Best Buy , which is $19 shy of their best price to date ( Target also has them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review .

If you want over-ears and are comfortable going without active noise cancellation, the are on sale starting at $79.99 ($120 off) at Amazon and Target — a new low price. The headphones are a noticeable improvement over their predecessor, delivering more detailed sound and support for lossless audio. They also last up to 50 hours on a single charge, while their memory foam ear cushions make them comfortable enough for long listening sessions. Read our review.

The are down to around $89.95 ($80 off) at Amazon , Best Buy , and Target , nearly matching their lowest price to date. The wireless earbuds feature a slick, eye-catching transparent option and solid noise cancellation, especially at this price. They’re also exceptionally comfortable, with four ear tip sizes to help you find a secure fit. Sure, you don’t get wireless charging, but they offer IPX4 water resistance and up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge. Read our review .

The recently released 16.3-inch MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage is on sale starting at $3,099 ($300 off) — a new low price — at Amazon . The redesigned laptop is Apple’s first with an OLED touchscreen, which allows for rich colors and deep blacks. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications. Read our review .

The 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is on sale starting at $1,749 ($250 off) at Amazon and Best Buy , which is a new low price. The Pro builds on its predecessor with a faster chip and support for Wi-Fi 7. In our testing, it handled multitasking, photo editing, and occasional video editing with ease while still delivering exceptional battery life. It lacks the newer MacBook Pro’s gorgeous OLED display, but its Mini LED screen still looks great, especially given its smooth 120Hz refresh rate. It also offers excellent speakers and a good selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, and an SD card slot. Read our review .

Apple’s newest entry-level smartwatch remains our top recommendation for anyone who wants a basic fitness tracker, as it offers all the essentials alongside an always-on display and Apple’s S10 chip, which enables on-device Siri requests. Read our review .

title: Purse found of woman, 24, swept from California beach three weeks ago
author: Keely Aouga
text:
Se Nah Park was overwhelmed by a wave at the notorious Panther Beach

The purse of a 24-year-old who was swept into the ocean at a notorious California beach three weeks ago was found on Wednesday, as the west coast saw record high king tides.

The Santa Cruz county sheriff’s office confirmed that Se Nah Park’s purse was found by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach, south of Panther Beach, where she was swept away into the ocean on 8 November.

According to a GoFundMe started by Park’s friends, Park and five others had gathered around a bonfire beyond the “keyhole” archway at Panther Beach that night.

Four members of the group, including Park, attempted to make their way back through the keyhole when a powerful wave struck, sweeping Park into the ocean.

The three individuals managed to get back up the cliffslide, but tragically, Park did not.

Three weeks later, Park’s body has not been located yet, but the discovery of her purse may lead her community closer towards locating her body. .

The coast guard suspended the active search efforts to find Park on 9 November.

“Given the extensive search effort of the surrounding area and environmental conditions, we have suspended active search efforts pending further developments,” Lt Max Holloway, Sector San Francisco search and rescue mission coordinator, said at the time.

“We worked closely with our partner agencies and exhausted all available resources in our attempt to locate Ms Park. Our deepest condolences are with her family and loved ones,” the statement concluded.

In the weeks since, Park’s family and friends have not given up on their search efforts.

Her family and friends continue to “hold on to the hope that Senah can be found and brought home to rest”, her friends shared in a message on GoFundMe.

Black Friday is here, and if you want a little help keeping your floors clean this holiday season, now is a great time to pick up a robot vacuum. Some of the best models we’ve tested over the last year or two are on sale for up to 60 percent off, whether you’re after a basic robovac for quick cleanups or a more advanced model that vacuums, mops, and practically takes care of itself.

This year’s sale has made some pricier robot vacuums a lot more affordable. The Eufy Omni C28 , for example, now costs about what you’d expect to pay for a budget bot, while the Matic — which impressed us with its almost humanlike navigation — is getting a rare discount in the form of a bundle. Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock.

The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

The Narwal Flow 2 is an excellent robot vacuum for hardwood floors. A superb mop with a wide flat roller pad and a good vacuum, the Flow 2 also has top-notch navigation and obstacle detection. Its sleek base station is also less of an eyesore than most models. Read our review.

It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.

Ecovacs’ robot vacuum and mop can pretreat stains, keep carpets dry with a smart mop cover, and deliver powerful 22,000Pa suction. It also includes an all-in-one dock that automatically empties the dustbin, refills the water tanks, and washes the mop with heated, pressurized water.

The Matter-compatible SwitchBot K11 Plus is ideal for small apartments, bedrooms, and home offices. It can easily navigate around chair and desk legs and into tight spaces that most other bots miss. It also features a commendable 6,000Pa of suction power — which is great for this price point — and works well on both hardwood and carpet.

With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum-mop hybrid. While its 20,000Pa suction isn’t quite as powerful as the X60 Ultra’s and it can’t tackle especially high thresholds as well, it’s still an excellent option. Its edge cleaning also isn’t quite as effective as the X60 Ultra’s, but you’re otherwise getting many of the same features for a lot less.

The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 delivers powerful 25,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a self-cleaning dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop, and refills its water tanks. Unlike the X50 Ultra, however, it lacks the ability to climb high thresholds or stairs.

The Freo X Ultra features spinning triangular mop pads and can swing slightly to reach baseboards. Its large charging dock holds two big water tanks, while Narwal’s disposable onboard bin compresses the dust. It’s also relatively quiet when it returns to the dock, and its anti-tangle brush and 8,200Pa of suction perform well on most carpets.

Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better. Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are available during Black Friday at Best Buy for $169, their lowest price yet from a major retailer. There are upsides and downsides to this model: They feature improved noise cancellation thanks to more mics, despite using the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but they can’t fold up as compactly, making them a little bigger to pack in your bag. Either one you choose, you’ll have some great headphones to listen to going into 2027.

Playtronic Games is getting ready to launch Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition as a free update on PlayStation 5, Switch 2, and PC on December 15th. Unfortunately for Xbox owners, the developer says it “can’t commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future.” In a statement posted on X , Playtronic said that it understands the frustration some players may feel, but that bringing the Definitive Edition to Xbox just isn’t viable “given the technological challenges and costs,” and reminded people that they’re a small team.

Some, like The Game Business editor-in-chief Christopher Dring , have speculated that Xbox’s smaller install base has made it harder for some indie devs to “financially justify” launching on Xbox. Others, like John Linneman of Digital Foundry , have countered that Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is ultimately a minor update and pointed out that the Xbox Series X version was already available in native 4K, unlike the PS4 and Switch versions.

title: OpenAI countersues Apple for allegedly stealing trade secrets
author: Reuters
text:
Lawsuit also alleging pressure on hardware suppliers comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching employees

OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the company of ⁠stealing its trade secrets ​and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices.

The suit, filed in northern California federal court, comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.

OpenAI filed the counterclaims ⁠in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple’s employment practices were designed to “trap” employees and prevent them from working on competitors’ technology.

OpenAI is developing AI-enabled personal electronic devices that threaten to “outcompete Apple on what ⁠Apple views as its own turf”, the company said in its Friday court filing.

OpenAI said in the filing that Apple ​gained confidential information by rehiring a former employee who worked ‌at OpenAI for six months. In ‌that time, the employee gained access to specific information on a new device as well as OpenAI’s roadmap for future hardware ‌products.

“Given the timing, it now appears that stealing those documents may have been his reason for joining OpenAI in the first place,” OpenAI said.

Apple denied using the rehired employee to access OpenAI’s confidential information and denied trying to suppress competition in AI device manufacturing.

“OpenAI’s counterclaims are a transparent attempt to distract from the substance of Apple’s lawsuit,” Apple said in a Friday statement.

Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for ‌talent and proprietary technology.

Apple sued OpenAI and the former Apple employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu in July, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner’s foray into consumer hardware.

Tan, ​a 24-year Apple employee who was a vice-president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch, was part of the group that launched the AI device startup io Products before it was acquired by OpenAI in 2025.

OpenAI and the employees have denied those allegations and said that Apple’s lawsuit depended on its unauthorized monitoring of Liu’s personal messages after he stopped working for Apple. OpenAI and ⁠attorneys for Tan and Liu did not immediately respond to a request for comment on ​Friday’s court filing.

In Friday’s filing, OpenAI criticized ​Apple for encouraging employees to do work on ​their personal Apple devices and accounts, then preventing those employees from an orderly separation of work and ​personal accounts when they leave ‌for new jobs.

OpenAI said ​that Apple continues to access ​former employees’ personal devices and accounts after they leave the company, enabling Apple to “monitor and ensnare departing employees” when they leave for competitors.

OpenAI said that 400 employees have left Apple for OpenAI so far, and Apple wants to intimidate other employees from leaving to find other tech companies.

title: Charity set up by Captain Tom Moore’s family applies to be struck off
author: Nadeem Badshah
text:
Watchdog had found ‘repeated’ misconduct by veteran’s daughter and her husband in running the foundation

A charity set up by the family of the pandemic fundraiser Captain Sir Tom Moore has applied to be struck off.

The charity is now known as the 1189808 Foundation, having dropped Moore’s name at the request of his family last year.

An application to have the organisation struck off appeared on the Companies House register on Friday.

The dropping of the captain’s name came after the charities watchdog found there had been “repeated” misconduct and mismanagement on the part of the second world war veteran’s daughter and her husband in their running of the foundation.

The Charity Commission’s report published in 2024 found a “repeated pattern of behaviour” through which Hannah Ingram-Moore and her husband, Colin, made private gains and which the regulator said would have left people feeling “misled”.

The report found that a £1.4m book deal and an £18,000 awards ceremony appearance fee were among the financial benefits the Ingram-Moores enjoyed through their family links to the Captain Tom Foundation, which was launched in May 2020.

The Ingram-Moores have already been banned from being charity trustees, and Hannah Ingram-Moore was prohibited from being a trustee or holding a senior management role in any charity in England and Wales for 10 years, and Colin Ingram-Moore for eight years.

Moore became a household name during the first Covid-19 lockdown, raising £39.4m for NHS charities by walking laps of the garden at his home in Marston Moretaine, Bedfordshire. He was honoured with a knighthood from Queen Elizabeth II.

The millions raised and donated to NHS Charities Together for its Covid-19 Urgent Appeal before the foundation was formed were not part of the commission’s inquiry.

Moore, a father of two who was born in Keighley, West Yorkshire, died aged 100 in February 2021 after testing positive for coronavirus.

title: Mercedes' early advantage is even scarier than it looks
author: Josh Suttill
text:
Mercedes has been the benchmark 2026 team, but given it’s only won one of the last six races, what’s behind its dominant start to Formula 1’s Qatar Grand Prix weekend?

World champion Kimi Antonelli led a Mercedes one-two in both practice sessions, four and a half tenths clear of the nearest competition on single-lap pace in FP2 - despite their fastest laps being set on mediums.

Reading into the final classification is a messy endeavour given two red flags disrupted run plans but it actually makes Mercedes’ position even more formidable.

Russell got very close to completing a full lap on softs but did not finish the lap in time - still, his theoretical fastest lap (taking the two sectors he did do on the faster tyre) was some 0.835 seconds faster than the quickest non-Mercedes, Max Verstappen’s Red Bull.

Theoretical best laps FP2 Russell 1m22.683sVerstappen +0.835sPiastri +0.866sHamilton +1.284s

Mercedes’ advantage was also sizeable when looking at the adjusted long-run pace in FP2. You can slice such analysis multiple ways but accounting for laps in traffic as best as possible Antonelli leads the way, a whopping 0.810 seconds faster per lap than Verstappen's Red Bull.

Antonelli (Mercedes) 1m28.074s Russell (Mercedes) +0.205s

Verstappen (Red Bull) +0.810s Hadjar (Red Bull) +1.058s

Norris (McLaren) +1.061s Piastri (McLaren) +1.173s

*Ferrari didn’t complete a representative long run

Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin called it “one of our better Fridays this year” while deputy Mercedes team boss Bradley Lord said Mercedes “hit the ground running” as the car “seems to suit this circuit”.

Lord said there were “very minimal differences” between Antonelli and Russell’s set-ups by the end of the day, with them looking closely matched over both single laps and longer runs. Russell had made some, in his words, “good changes” after FP1 that made him comfortable with the balance.

Lord said the car is “competitive in both the high speed and the low speed. One of the question marks we had was the low-speed performance with the new update [introduced in Malaysia].

“Obviously, this circuit bias is towards the medium and high speed where we know we've definitely made gains.

“So we're making good use of that. Then hopefully it just reflects our ongoing learning about how to get the most out of the car with this package on it.”

So there is an element of Qatar playing to the strengths of the package and nullifying the effect of the Malaysia upgrade having put the car in a narrower performance window, for low-speed corners in particular - even if Mercedes has made gains since then in widening it.

There are far fewer heavy braking zones or tricky corner entries like Mexico, where the W17 struggled more.

The Mercedes drivers, by and large, avoided the balance issues that have been plaguing rivals like Red Bull in Qatar.

“They find the key to fix this balance, and this balance issue we can have here by having a massive front limitation in high-speed, medium-speed corners, without compromising the entry,” Red Bull’s technical director Pierre Wache observed.

“They are able to do that, and we have the work to do to achieve better.”

Plus, the cars are fairly energy-starved in Qatar - particularly through the high-speed corners and main straight - so the efficiency of Mercedes’ energy management package is rewarded here, as it was in Monza and Baku.

But the fact it still has a significant advantage over McLaren (with that same power unit) and Red Bull (also with a very strong power unit) suggests it has a lot to do with Mercedes’s strength in high-speed corners and it finding a strong car balance that its rivals can’t.

Where Red Bull and McLaren are struggling

Max Verstappen has won four of the last six races, but he was struggling with some familiar problems with his RB22.

He suffered team radio issues early in FP1 that were later resolved, but a “disconnected” balance problem remained throughout Friday.

“It's quite a unique track. It's not an easy track to get things right, so I hope we can do a little bit better,” Verstappen said.

“The gap to Mercedes is very big, so we need a big jump for that. But I think already from our side, if we can get that balance more together, that's probably already half of the laptime that we're losing.”

Verstappen also complained of “heavy steering” in FP2 with Wache admitting, “The car is struggling here a lot in terms of kerbing and stuff that will damage. We have to fix that.”

McLaren’s also wary of the fragility of its car as it started the day on its older specification of floor before switching the drivers onto the new floor introduced in Las Vegas.

“Many people can run off and damage parts, so we just made sure that we didn't damage any of the new spec for this car,” McLaren’s senior racing director Randy Singh explained.

McLaren’s power unit exploitation deficit to Mercedes and known baked-in 2026 missteps like short gear ratios explain some of its gap to Mercedes, who Norris said are “just a different level compared to everyone this weekend”.

“It shows just in general how far off we are.

“It's not like something works better for them here. I mean, you can just clearly see if they're quick here, they're quick in a lot of other places for the same reason.

“So I think it's more a realisation of where we stand relative to them.”

The time loss is most visible on the run to Turn 1, where Norris tops out at 322km/h compared to Antonelli’s 332km/h and has already lost 0.175s by the exit of that corner.

It’s also present in the high-speed corners at Turn 12-15 where Norris loses another 0.125s, as the more planted Mercedes stretches its legs.

The Red Bull ends up leaking even more time there as Verstappen loses over three tenths there alone to Antonelli.

Mercedes has its eye on Red Bull as the “next team”, but Lord said he wouldn’t be surprised to see a five or six-car battle for pole position on Saturday.

There’s clearly one front-running team at risk of being excluded from that fight in Qatar.

What happened to ‘outlier’ Ferrari?

The outlier among the top teams on Friday was Ferrari as its drivers didn’t even manage to complete a representative long-run in FP2. Charles Leclerc spun while Lewis Hamilton stopped on-track with a power unit problem.

“It's been just a very, very difficult session,” Leclerc admitted after FP2.

“When I lost the car, it probably made it even worse, so we just decided to change the floor, which cost us quite a bit of time.

“But to be honest, this is not even the reason why we were slow. We were just very slow from the first lap this morning to the last lap in FP2, and it's very difficult to understand what is the outlier.

“I think not only for us but for everybody, particularly comparing to Mercedes, that seems to be, they always kind of had the best car, but now it's to an extent that we did not expect.”

As you can see from a comparison of their fastest FP2 laps, Leclerc’s laptime bleed to Antonelli is consistent throughout the lap.

And even on their fastest theoretical laps, there’s major losses in all three of his best sectors - 0.570s in sector one, 0.443s in sector two and 0.484s in sector three.

That’s likely to lead to a long night of head-scratching from Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren as to why Mercedes appears to be in a different league in Qatar and whether there’s any chance of anyone catching it.

Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game.

The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. At $599, though, the new Mini is still relatively expensive if you mainly want a tablet for browsing the web or streaming shows. The last-gen iPad Mini, which runs on Apple’s A17 Pro chip, is available for under $500 if you’d rather save another $100 and can live without the OLED screen and water resistance. But if you’ve been waiting for a more worthwhile upgrade to Apple’s smallest tablet, the current Black Friday discount makes the new model easier to justify.

title: Thousands still without power after storms that snarled Thanksgiving travel
author: Edward Helmore and agencies
text:
Homes without power, travel disrupted and Macy’s Thanksgiving parade postponed for first time in New York

Storms have flooded communities on the US east coast, knocking out power to nearly a million customers and prompting the first-ever postponement of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City.

High winds and flooding hammered both coasts, disrupting holiday travel. More than 900,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday evening, with the majority in east coast states, according to the outage tracking website PowerOutage.us. More than 2,200 flights to or from US destinations were delayed and more than 400 were cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.

Macy’s postponed the annual Thanksgiving parade until Saturday because of concerns about how the parade’s large balloons would fare in the windswept canyons between Manhattan’s skyscrapers.

Torrential rain, high winds and flooding pounded sections of the east coast. New Jersey was under a state of emergency, along with parts of New York. The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia to most of the mid-Atlantic and southern New England.

People were rescued from their cars in New York City because of flooding, said the mayor, Zohran Mamdani, and similar rescues were reported in other coastal communities.

“There is no destination worth your safety,” Mamdani said.

Strong winds and flooding disrupted train lines, toppled trees and caused power outages on Thanksgiving night, New York City emergency management officials said. Several scaffolding structures collapsed in the wind, but no injuries were reported.

The storms also flooded areas from North Carolina through to New Jersey as high tide rolled in. Roads were closed, and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.

Avalon, New Jersey, was seeing some of the worst flooding in its history, said Scott J Wahl, the borough’s business administrator.

“Not quite Hurricane Sandy,” Wahl said, referring to the benchmark storm for his village on the far south end of New Jersey’s Atlantic coast.

Flood waters washed debris over the road, and a few drivers were rescued after driving around barricades into the waters, but no injuries were reported, Wahl said.

Lance Miller, 54, said flood waters in his Ocean City, New Jersey, neighbourhood were about a foot deep and that driving to the nearest supermarket would probably “destroy your car”.

Miller said he would be staying indoors and having Thanksgiving dinner with his wife and daughter. But he said some of his friends were “not so lucky” and had flooding inside their homes.

The Margate City fire department near Atlantic City, New Jersey posted video on Facebook of water pouring through the city’s streets, even before heavy rains started.

A firefighter said the tide was coming in ferociously, even with an hour to go before its peak. Water closed in on houses, and sandbags were piled in front of businesses.

Some highways and bridges were temporarily closed. The nearly 18-mile (29-km) Chesapeake Bay bridge-tunnel in southern Virginia was closed for several hours on Thursday morning because of high winds, while NC 12, the only highway connecting Hatteras Island on the North Carolina Outer Banks to the mainland, was closed after seawater breached the dunes and covered the two-lane highway.

In Maryland, nearly 2 million water customers in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties were asked to conserve water because of intermittent power disruptions associated with the storm. Baltimore police closed several streets on Thursday night after storm surge caused flooding in waterfront neighborhoods.

The storms also prompted several brief tornado warnings on Thursday, including a rare twister south-east of Seattle, Washington.

The US president, Donald Trump, signed a disaster declaration on Thursday for Florida in response to earlier flooding that damaged hundreds of homes and required water rescues. Trump had approved funding earlier this week, but gathered local officials on Thanksgiving to talk about it in a small signing ceremony at his home in West Palm Beach.

Trump was asked about aid for Thursday’s storms on the east coast. “Well, we’re going to look at that. We have some requests from others,” he said.

Heavy snow fell on parts of Illinois and Missouri with St Louis recording 7.3in (18.5cm) of snowfall. Sainte Genevieve, Missouri, recorded 14in.

The ice arena in Wentzville, Missouri, which hosts hockey and other ice skating activities, was empty when the roof caved in at about 3 am, according to the city.

Meanwhile, high-tide driven waves and strong winds caused flooding along the Pacific coast on Thursday. The conditions were expected into Friday, according to the National Weather Service.

Record tides along the California coast forced evacuations in areas from Humboldt county in the far north to Ventura county near Los Angeles.

King tides were surging along the west coast.

Video showed a big wave tearing down part of the Pacifica pier in California on Wednesday, sending it into the ocean. Officials had closed the L-shaped pier in the summer after finding cracks.

Amtrak’s Pacific Surfliner posted more than a dozen itinerary changes on social media on Thursday morning, starting with one that said trains could not run through San Clemente “due to track damage”. It also suspended service between Irvine and Oceanside because of washouts caused by high tide conditions. Service was further shut down from San Diego north to Oceanside and up to Los Angeles international airport.

title: The explosion of extreme wealth is the major problem of our time | Bernie Sanders
author: Bernie Sanders
text:
At this pivotal moment in American history, let us move forward together to take on and defeat a powerful, greedy and corrupt ruling class

W e are at a pivotal moment in history. Never before in human history have so few people held so much wealth and so much power. And never before have we seen such an unprecedented level of greed, arrogance and irresponsibility on the part of the world’s ruling class.

Here is the good news: leaders from around the world are finally starting to wake up. This week, elected officials and economists from around the world – including four Nobel prize winners – came together in Paris for a “Summit Against International Oligarchy”. As the summit’s proclamation stated, “The explosion of extreme wealth is the major social fact of our time … We are sounding the alarm: billionaires are a threat to our democracies.”

They are right. And that is exactly why I organized, along with other progressives, the Fight Oligarchy tour last year which brought out more than 340,000 Americans in 27 states.

As members of the summit point out, in 1987 the wealth of the richest 0.0001% amounted to the equivalent of 3% of global gross domestic product (GDP). Since then, these 3,000 households have seen their fortunes grow to 17% of global GDP.

At this moment, we live in a world where the top 1% owns more wealth than the bottom 95% of humanity and the gap between the very rich and the poor is growing wider and wider.

Think about it. After all of the wars and revolutions over the last 250 years, after all of the carefully drafted constitutions and hard-fought elections, after all of the wonderful speeches that politicians around the world have given, the top 1% owns more wealth than the bottom 95% of humanity.

In country after country, we are seeing unprecedented income and wealth inequality.

We see it in America today, where the top 1% now owns more wealth than the bottom 93% and one man, Elon Musk, owns more wealth than the bottom 53% of American households.

We see it in Russia, where the latest figures indicate that the wealthiest 500 people in that country control more wealth than the bottom 99.8% of their people.

We see it in France, where more than one out of five children live in poverty, while 53 billionaires own more wealth than the bottom half of the population.

We see it in Africa, where in recent years, nearly 850 million people have struggled with food insecurity, while just four men own more wealth than the bottom 50% of the people on that continent. Yes. Four men own more wealth than half a continent.

We see it in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, where a handful of families have unbelievable wealth and power while most of the work done in those countries is performed by impoverished and powerless migrant laborers.

But it’s not just massive income and wealth inequality. It is oligarchs’ control over the global economy. It is oligarchs’ control over much of the media and what people see, hear and read. It is oligarchs avoiding taxes by stashing trillions of dollars in offshore tax havens around the world while the children in their native countries go hungry.

And what are the political implications when the very rich get much richer while working people struggle and feel more and more powerless?

The answer is clear. If people no longer believe that their government is responding to their needs, many of them will give up on democracy and move towards authoritarianism.

And it’s not just Trumpism in the United States. It’s the growth of extreme rightwing parties in Germany, France, the UK and elsewhere.

All over the world, people are asking a very simple question: why should I continue to vote for the same old, same old political parties when my job has been shipped overseas, my factory has been automated, my credit card interest rate is now 25%, I’m unable to retire with dignity, and my children will likely have a lower standard of living than I do – all while the top 1% have never, ever had it so good?

As the country the most billionaires, with a record 989, including 15 of the top 20, the US has a major role to play.

Bottom line: if we are going to improve the lives of working people and protect democracy, the new Democratic majority can no longer continue the failed status quo policies that have devastated so many of our people throughout our country.

This election was about change, real change, and that’s what Democrats must deliver. Now is the time to take on Big Money and fight for an economy that works for all, not just a few.

Yes. We need a wealth tax on billionaires to substantially reduce child poverty, build affordable housing, protect our seniors and invest in the needs of working families.

Yes. We need to guarantee healthcare as a human right by passing Medicare for All.

Yes. We must raise the minimum wage to a living wage – at least $20 an hour – and make it easier for workers to join unions by passing the Pro Act.

Yes. We must strengthen public education and make higher education available to all, regardless of income.

Yes. We must make sure that AI and robotics benefit working families and not just enrich a handful of big tech oligarchs.

Yes. We must ensure that everyone in America can retire with dignity by expanding social security, scrapping the cap on taxable income and restoring traditional defined benefit pension plans.

The new Democratic majority in Congress must act boldly and with an unprecedented sense of urgency. The crises facing our country and the world are much too dangerous to be ignored, or to be dealt with through tepid half-measures.

At this pivotal moment in American history, let us move forward together to take on and defeat a powerful, greedy and corrupt ruling class.

Bernie Sanders is a US senator, and ranking member of the health, education, labor and pensions committee. He represents the state of Vermont and is the longest-serving independent in the history of Congress

title: 'It's always sour to lose' admits Tibor Del Grosso after going second to Thibau Nys in Ostrava at World Cup opener
author: Ben Goddard
text:
The 23-year-old was battling for victory on the last lap with rival Thibau Nys (Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions), but came out second best in the first duel of the season between the pair.

Del Grosso said that he felt ‘sour’ losing to his Belgian rival after conceding the lead and failing to regain the front position in the snow during the final corners, while Nys stayed on the firmer ground.

“I don't think it was a bad performance, if you're close to winning. Of course, it's always sour to lose,” said Del Grosso afterwards to organisers.

“It was just a matter of having the lead and keeping the lead going into the last corner, at some point Thibau [Nys] came with quite some speed. I felt like there were some opportunities after, to still overtake him, but then I waited maybe a bit too long.

“The bit towards the final corner, there was only really one path where you could ride in. I tried to overtake, didn't really go anywhere.”

Del Grosso announced that he will ride 13 races this cyclo-cross season – all of the 12 World Cup rounds and the World Championships in Oostend.

Last season the Dutchman came into his first elite season from the under-23 ranks and finished 14th in his opening race at the World Cup round at Namur in mid-December. Before racing in Ostrava, the 23-year-old joked that a 13th place finish Friday would be an improvement of last year's first race.

“I think a lot of people think about my [cyclo-cross] races from last season,” said Del Grosso. “Last year I also needed some time to get into it. I didn’t prepare to be here in my best shape.”

Del Grosso looked comfortable on the slippery terrain in Ostrava and was able to follow Nys before putting his rival under pressure in the final laps.

“I have mixed feelings, I can be quite happy with my race today. The feeling was not yet where it was supposed to be. It was a really tactical race with how the course was. I think I played it relatively well, but then the final two minutes was not perfect," he reflected.

“I don't think it was a bad performance. Technically, I think it's a good 'cross. Some points for improvement, but also not crazy. A lot better than last year.”

Del Grosso competed on the road this season with Alpecin-Premier Tech and won the NXT Classic in April then adding 14th in Amstel Gold Race. The Dutchman took a two-month break following his last road race in the Flandrien Classic and National Coach Gerben de Knegt believed that it has allowed the youngster to ‘rest and train well’.

He told : "His road season has been somewhat disappointing for various reasons. He rested well and trained well. In other years, he also started the [cyclo-cross] season quite quickly after his road campaign.

“Now he is better prepared because he has been able to train for more weeks between the end of the road season and the start of his cyclo-cross winter.”

title: 100% wear in 15 laps - Qatar tyre issue has got even worse
author: Jon Noble
text:
Despite the highest front tyre pressures of the season and a maximum stint length already in place, Pirelli is evaluating if further precautions are needed for the Qatar Grand Prix after Friday practice served up “surprise after surprise.”

The Lusail circuit is already the most challenging of the season for tyres, but the evidence from the first day of track running has shown graining, wear and degradation to be at higher levels than anticipated pre-event.

It is suspected this has been caused by a more weathered track surface and the reduced downforce levels of the 2026 cars that are causing sliding.

On a weekend where there is a much-talked-about 27-lap maximum stint length laid down for each set of tyres, Pirelli has already seen evidence of the most abused front-left sets hitting 100% wear in localised areas after just 15 laps of running on Friday.

Pirelli’s chief engineer Simone Berra said: “It's quite impressive the surprises that this circuit gives to us every time they come here.”

Graining has been encountered on all three compounds - with it particularly aggressive on the C2 and C3. This is accelerating the wear in two specific areas of the tyre - near the inside shoulder and then on the very outside shoulder.

And it is in these specific areas where early analysis has pointed to some wear indicators having hit the 100% level after just 15 laps of high-fuel running in practice.

These elements are also contributing to Qatar producing levels of thermal decay degradation not seen in the past - up to 0.2 seconds per lap - which is going to have an impact on strategies as drivers will not be able to keep pushing on with stints as they have in the past.

On top of all this, Pirelli has also found evidence of gravel cuts in rubber that was returned to it after Friday practice.

Berra said: “We have seen some of them quite deep into the construction. There was also a red flag due to this, and it's something that obviously in a circuit like this, it's an additional variable that can create some attention from our side in terms of punctures.”

Gravel stone cuts discovered after Friday practice last year prompted Pirelli to increase tyre pressures ahead of Saturday running - and a repeat response has not been ruled out right now.

“We are evaluating all the variables,” he said. “If necessary, we will increase the pressure.”

Front pressures are currently at the 29psi set before the weekend, which is the highest they have ever been heading into an event and at the same level Pirelli settled on from Saturday onwards in Qatar last year.

If Pirelli chooses to raise the pressures any more, then they will be the highest they have been in the modern era of F1.

However, Berra is well aware that raising pressures will likely serve to reduce the contact patch of the tyres even more which could potentially increase graining even more.

“That's why I wouldn't increase the pressure if possible,” he said. “But if we have to for integrity reasons, obviously we are going to evaluate it.”

The other action Pirelli is considering in response to the findings about extreme wear of the tyres is reducing the maximum stint length from its current 27 laps.

Berra said that analysis would take place in Pirelli’s laboratory on the tyres used on Friday to see if there are any concerns about their integrity.

“We are going to check them, to section them, and obviously if there is no integrity issue, we will keep the 27 laps in any case because we know that graining level will reduce for the race, and the teams will do much more management to extend the stint length.

“It's an analysis that is ongoing in our laboratory and, with our usual prescription review, we are going to understand if we continue with 27 or not.”

Even if the situation is a marginal one, reducing the stint length may not necessarily be needed because, with degradation in play, Pirelli’s analysis is that it would make no sense for teams to run the maximum distance anyway as it would be too slow.

Instead, with the race distance being 57 laps it is much more logical for teams to split their stints in three equal ones of 19 laps.

However, teams could be forced to shuffle things around based on the timing of safety cars. So even if they headed into the race not intending to run tyres to the maximum distance, they could be tempted to trying to eke out a final 27-lap stint if safety car timing fell that way.

Berra thinks however that the degradation levels seen mean that pace-wise it would not make sense to run for 27 laps - and early safety cars would more likely turn the race into a three-stopper.

title: Blue Jays sign former Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr.
author: Andrew Mearns
text:
Jazz moves to Toronto after two and a half years in the Bronx.

If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The moment that the Yankees decided to pass on giving free agent second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. the one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer, his fate was all but set in stone. It was almost the exact same situation as a couple years ago with Gleyber Torres, who also had a perfectly reasonable case to at least be given the option of returning to New York on a one-year, make-good QO. But for one reason or another, the Yankees’ front office came to the conclusion that they were at the end of the rope with Gleyber, and the same has come to fruition with Jazz.

Chisholm found a new home today and it’s still in the AL East: Toronto. The Blue Jays came to terms with the second baseman on a one-year, $18.5 million deal for 2027 ($12.5 million in salary plus a $6 million signing bonus) that also has a funky option for 2028. It’s a $16 million player option, but if Jazz declines it, then the Jays still have a chance to bring him back on a pretty big $40 million club option. If they decline that and give him a $1.5 million buyout, then he’s a free agent next offseason as well. So if Jazz has a great year for Toronto and thinks he could beat $16 million, then Toronto still has a chance to bring him back on a hefty price tag, albeit hefty for just one year. The bottom line is that he’s locked into $34.5 million even if he repeats his up-and-down 2026 or regresses.

FanSided’s Robert Murray was the first to report the deal, and The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal had the specifics on the terms.

Chisholm’s 2026 campaign with the Yankees was a bit of a mess and we don’t need to go back into it in great detail. It was a disappointing walk year and we subsequently gave it a poor grade in our report card series. In a vaccum, Jazz was still productive in 2026 (a 98 wRC+ and good defense per FanGraphs still gave him 3.5 fWAR), but his slugging tumbled from a 30/30 guy in 2025 with .491 SLG to 19 homers with a .399 SLG. That looks bad when mixed in with his worst strikeout rates since 2023, and his highest in any season of at least 400 plate apperances. Still, Chisholm stole 41 bases as well and it’s not hard to envision a scenario where he becomes a pest again next year. It’s a reasonable gamble from Toronto’s perspective, and even if you’re tired with Jazz’s bit, the prospect of “Anthony Volpe, 2027 Yankees second baseman” isn’t particularly enthralling, either.

The high-variance outcomes at the plate seem to have alarmed the Yankees, and they probably also weren’t entirely thrilled by other incidents surrounding him. Your mileage may vary on them, but I know that I was personally more annoyed by unapologetic postgame quote after a brutal postseason error than the lollipop incident , which was just goofy. Jazz is Jazz. The Blue Jays’ fans will find this to be true as well. Now, will he come closer to the superlative 2025 version or the chaotic 2026 version?

We’ll learn the answer from a distance — but not too much of a distance. I’ve already made my guess.

title: Winners & losers from F1 2026 Qatar GP Friday practice
author: Scott Mitchell-Malm
text:
Kimi Antonelli led Mercedes team-mate George Russell in both Friday Formula 1 practice sessions for the 2026 Qatar Grand Prix, including an FP2 that was punctuated by two red flags.

Some drivers struggled more than others - and a few lost considerable running over the opening practice sessions - but who are the winners and losers from Friday in Qatar?

Loser: Ferrari (7th & 8th)

If you ask Charles Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton pulling over to the side of the road with a power issue in FP2 was likely the least of Ferrari's worries!

Hamilton was running an older engine for practice, so Leclerc seemed unperturbed by the issue. The bigger problem is that the "pace has just been very, very poor", reckons Leclerc.

"We were just very slow from the first lap this morning to the last lap in FP2 and it's very difficult to understand what is the outlier."

It didn't help that time was wasted changing Leclerc's floor after a spin, but that just distracted from what is Ferrari's real issue. It's slow by any measure and has a big night to try and fix it.

Pirelli’s rubber is taking a battering around the Qatar track - which has sealed its status as the most challenging of the season for tyres.

The Lusail venue delivers graining, high wear, high carcass temperatures because of the fast corners and fatigue risks, plus extra jeopardy caused by gravel stones - and this year things are worse than predicted pre-event.

A combination of the weathered track surface that has got rougher allied to 2026 downforce and performance levels have come together to produce high levels of localised graining that is resulting in some sets reaching 100% wear in localised areas after just 15 laps.

Despite the highest tyre pressures of the season, and a 27-lap maximum stint length for each set having been laid down, Pirelli is conducting analysis tonight to see if even more action needs to be taken ahead of qualifying day to avoid any risk of trouble in the race.

Winner: Mercedes (1st & 2nd)

After two consecutive weekends without a podium finish since wrapping up both its world championships, Mercedes looks in a mega place to end that mini streak here.

It could hardly have hoped for a better Friday. It looks very well balanced, strong in all corner types, and there's a massive one-lap advantage and in the long run too.

Both drivers seem pretty happy with how the car feels, and all of its rivals are worried and feel that Mercedes is in a league of its own.

So this is about as good as any weekend has looked for Mercedes in a long time.

Loser: Red Bull (5th & 6th)

Though Mercedes thinks Red Bull could emerge as its nearest rival come qualifying, right now this is miles off the standard that Red Bull and Max Verstappen have been setting in recent races.

There was a distinct air of unhappiness from the Red Bull camp on Friday evening, with Verstappen bemoaning a car that feels disconnected, a heavy steering problem needing resolving overnight, and just generally Red Bull not looking nearly as sorted with its car balance.

Technical director Pierre Wache is not optimistic that the gap can be closed significantly because it is so big. So this is looking like at the moment Red Bull suffering a chastening Friday that leaves it with lower hopes for the rest of the weekend than its recent mega form would have had it believing in coming into the weekend.

Winner: Racing Bulls (9th & 10th)

You might look at Racing Bulls' performance and think, hmm, leading the midfield as is pretty much usual, nothing to see here.

Peel back the layers and there's quite a lot more going on here.

Its biggest issue is straightline speed, but, as Liam Lawson puts it, that's all "stuff we can see and should be able to fix".

He says the team made a set-up change to an extent that is rarely seen between practice sessions in F1, which team boss Alan Permane confirmed was about adding more rotation into the car with most teams struggling with understeer.

"We already had quite a good car in P1 and now we have an even faster car," reckons Lawson, and the team has a big gap to the next team that only ran the mediums (Audi was closest but on the hards) on long runs.

Loser: Pierre Gasly (10th & 12th)

Gasly’s spin and subsequent beaching cost him valuable time in FP2, the session most representative of qualifying conditions.

The Frenchman said he “should have probably not gone for it” as the tyres were below temperature, he hit the kerbs, and then lost control of the car - damaging the car’s floor in the process. Furthermore he was “not fully pleased” with the set-up - and Alpine’s managing director Steve Nielsen said the balance is “nowhere near where it needs to be”.

This was never likely to be a great Alpine track given high-speed performance is its biggest weakness but now Gasly is even more on the back foot heading into Saturday.

Winner: Rafael Camara (15th & 17th)

Camara’s trouble-free Friday will come as a relief to the rookie who endured a rocky start to F1 in his home race.

In Qatar, Camara finished ahead of Haas team-mate Ollie Bearman but his long-run pace is of greater importance.

The Brazilian was right on par with Bearman in FP2, under a tenth slower than the Briton over his stint.

It’s looking like the most useful running yet in this cameo ahead of his full-season F1 debut.

Loser: Aston Martin (19th & 20th)

This is looking like a slightly better weekend for Aston Martin than in Las Vegas, but that comes with the extremely big asterisk that it couldn't really be worse.

As it stands, better might just mean not fighting with Cadillac. There are no long runs to be able to judge the team on partly because of the biggest issue of the day, which is that the car didn't seem particularly robust around the challenges of such a parts-breaking circuit.

Aston Martin opted to call it a day with all the disruptions in order to fix what it could, having had a lot of downtime between and during the sessions to try and repair damage.

Mike Krack predicted an evening bonding bits of carbon back together with glue, Lance Stroll has a back problem, and this looks like a tricky start to a weekend that Aston Martin had, in relative terms, slightly higher hopes for.

Loser: Williams (14th & 16th)

Williams hovered around P15 on Friday and neither driver started on the front foot, as both Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon had offs in FP1.

Sainz’s long run was faster than Albon’s on average, but the pair are well behind the rest of the midfield - our analysis putting Williams almost a second behind next-best team Audi and behind Haas.

The Spaniard said he failed to “close” his laps. “There's always snaps, always understeer, there's always a balance that maybe doesn't suit the whole lap and it's difficult to close it.”

That doesn’t bode well for qualifying.

title: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament
author: Keely Aouga
text:
Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’

A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, a sign of the strained relations between the neighboring countries.

Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it. The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”.

“He has been repeatedly abusive and insulting to Canadians,” May said as she formally introduced the petition, according to Politico .

She called Donald Trump’s envoy “the most undiplomatic diplomat” Canada had ever seen.

The petition accuses Hoekstra of “undermining” Canada-US diplomatic relations through repeated statements about Canadian politics that its signatories say are “inconsistent with diplomatic protocol”.

The US state department did not immediately return a request for comment.

Hoekstra is a deeply polarizing figure in Canada, particularly for his response to Trump’s desire to annex the country and make Canada the 51st US state.

Speaking to a Michigan radio station last year, he described the president’s rhetoric as a “sign of affection” and questioned why Canadians were offended by what he characterized as a “generous offer”.

Hoekstra also previously described Canada’s 2025 federal election that saw a remarkable come-from-behind victory for the prime minister’s Liberal party as “anti-American”.

The US ambassador had suggested Canada could be blamed if Republicans performed poorly in this month’s midterm elections.

“That’s an interesting way of framing it,” Carney replied, when asked about the comments.

Democrats swept the November elections, including key Senate races in border states such as Michigan and Maine, where the bitter tariff war between Washington and Ottawa has hit residents hard.

Last month Carney said American tariffs hurt both American and Canadian households. He added that auto exports to the US had so far fallen 10%, and US exports to Canada have fallen by more than 20%.

“US tariffs have upended a trade bargain that’s existed for decades,” Carney said. “They’ve raised costs for American families while putting Ontario workers and businesses at a disadvantage and under a cloud of uncertainty.”

Hoekstra had also accused Canada of potential “political interference” in the US election, a claim Carney said held “no merit”. Speaking to reporters in Turkey, the prime minister said he was “disappointed that their envoy sees that as his role, to make these suggestions”.

Even though the Canadian government is required to provide a formal response to the petition presented by May, the petition is nonbinding.

“I think the government will quite likely say, ‘No, we’re not prepared to declare Pete Hoekstra persona non grata and strip him of his diplomatic credentials,’”, May said in an interview with CTV .

Despite this possibility, May expects the petition to signal to Trump that the Canadian government has the support of its constituents, and she hopes the government can use it as leverage against Trump with Democrats holding power in Congress for the second half of Trump’s term.

title: Bad luck for Lucinda Brand with mechanical issues in snowy opening round of cyclo-cross World Cup in Ostrava
author: Ben Goddard
text:
The picturesque venue was a step into the unknown, with the Czech Republic hosting its first-ever World Cup event.

While the snow and Christmas lights made for a unique setting at the former coal mine venue, the frozen surface and deep ruts made for dangerous conditions. The evening race saw temperatures drop below freezing, and Brand was one of several casualties of the frozen ground.

At the halfway point, Brand was fighting in the top 10 before she couldn't clip into her pedals, a problem that many riders suffered during the elite women's and elite men's race.

For the Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions rider, though, she was left frustrated and shouting at her pit crew as they desperately tried to solve the issue from the pits.

Brand then lost over a minute and couldn't regain the time in the difficult conditions, finishing 15th and 2:25 behind race winner Marie Schreiber (SD Worx–Protime).

Brand was not the only rider to struggle with her equipment, as race winner Schreiber and third-placed finisher Manon Bakker were both forced to change bikes due to frozen pedals.

Despite having technical issues of her own, Bakker was hoping for more snow as the cyclo-cross World Cup continues in Tabor on Sunday.

“I made too many mistakes to really get into the win. I think everybody struggled with their pedals, I couldn’t clip in at all. I had a mechanical with my first bike and had to change, which is where I lost quite a lot of time," Bakker said.

“I came back, but that was it. I'd rather hope for more snow (at Tabor on Sunday). I think I'm the only one who was really smiling at the weather.”

It was Brand’s first outing in these snow conditions after missing previous World Cup rounds in Val di Sole.

“We haven’t had too often the chance for it,” said Brand on the snow conditions before the opening World Cup round. “I missed the World Cups in Val di Sole. This is something different again as there is not as much snow everywhere [on the course itself].”

Brand won the overall cyclo-cross World Cup series last year after sweeping the opening seven rounds in a commanding season.

However, this season the Dutch woman has found racing much closer and was beaten on two occasions last weekend by Sara Casasola. In the second of those races, Brand fell heavily at the X2O 'cross in Beringen and commented about suffering rib pain afterwards.

"My rib hurts a little. I now have to breathe well and calmly," Brand said. “It needs to heal again. It remains to be seen how this will develop in the coming days. You can do nothing but wait and let it recover.”

Brand won the World Cup overall by 97 points ahead of Aniek Van Alphen (777TV CX Team). However, with Van Alphen finishing runner-up in Ostrava, the pressure is on the two-time World Champion as they head to the second round in Tabor on Sunday.

title: World Cup Ostrava: Thibau Nys surges ahead of Tibor Del Grosso to triumph in elite men's snowy first round
author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
text:
Reigning European champion Thibau Nys (Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureau Lions) held off Dutch champion Tibor Del Grosso (Alpecin-Premier Tech) on the final corner and won the opening round of the UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup in Ostrava, Czech Republic.

Michael Vanthourenhout (Pauwels Sauzen-Altez Industriebouw Cycling Team) then nabbed the final spot on the podium with a final push through blowing snow ahead of of Cameron Mason (777tv CX Team) in fourth and Jente Michels (Alpecin-Premier Tech) in fifth.

Nys continued his string of victories, dominating the X2O Trofee series with a trio of wins this month and taking the ’cross continental title.

"It was a really difficult one, but I think it's in my top three of most beautiful cyclo-cross victories. I think the fans, the atmosphere, the chorus, the snow makes it one to remember," Nys told broadcasters at the finish.

Nys let out a loud scream as he crossed the line, only able to drop Del Grosso in the final 200 metres with a more powerful sprint. Nys admitted he overcame two slow leaks and pitted for a fresh bike twice, then used "good technique" to seal the victory.

"I had two flat tyres, so it kept pushing me a little bit back. I didn't lose a lot because it [tyre pressure] was slowly going out, but it kept pushing me a bit out of the race. And then when I found my way to the front, I tried to make a move and push hard. Then on the last lap, I managed it perfectly and did a good sprint," he noted.

"I was feeling way, way better than the last two weekends, just physically. But then of course you come here on a circuit where it's difficult to release the full power, so the fact that I can finish it off like this is a proof that my cyclo-cross skills are still there."

The World Cup season opened with two rounds in Czechia, the elite fields competing Friday in Ostrava in the only night races of the 12-round series. Floodlights illuminated a blanket of snow covering the venue, with the temperature holding steady for most of the afternoon at -1°C, but the wind chill making it feel five degrees colder.

Niels Vandeputte (Alpecin-Premier Tech Development) put on the power beside Nys from the start and took the front spot on the twisty course. Vanthourenhout and Del Grosso then led the long line of riders through the first pass of the finish line, riding in 6:36, which was the slowest lap of the nine.

There were narrow ruts instead of mud from the elite women’s race as the temperatures remained below freezing, and holiday lights sprinkled around the circuit. Amid the sounds of cowbells and cheers, the ringing of disc brakes was heard with constant speed changes as the track was slippery.

On the start of lap three, Gerben Kuypers (Pauwels Sauzen-Altez Industriebouw) took the lead ahead of Del Grosso and Pauwels teammate Vanthourenhout as small gaps began to form in the field of 75 riders.

At the mid-point of the contest, 10 riders settled in at the front - Del Grosso between the Pauwels Sauzen duo of Kuypers and Nieuwenhuis, then Vanthourenhout, Nys, Kuypers, Jent Michels, Yordi Corsus, Witse Meeussen, Felipe Orts and Cameron Mason.

It was Nys who drove the pace at the front to start the sixth and seventh laps, the second time carving a gap of five seconds to chasers across the stairs. However, he had to slow to bang one foot on the pedal to clear debris from his cleat and it was game-on again. Dutch ’cross champion Del Grosso, Vanthourenhout, Kuypers, Michels and Mason made it to his back wheel, but others were distanced for good.

On the final lap, Del Grosso took command at the front with Nys glued to his wheel, Vanthourenhout third and Mason in fourth. In a corner, Vanthourenhout dove to the front of the lead trio and held the position into the tricky descent from the stairs, while Nys made a pass of Del Grosso to nab second position. With the wind blowing light snow, Del Grosso and Nys went back into the front positions, Vanthourenhout losing momentum in a corner before the barriers. Nys made the pass before the short steps feature and drove the sprint to the line and keep his winning streak alive.

title: Mercedes set pace in eventful Qatar second practice
text:
World champion Kimi Antonelli set the pace ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell in a disrupted second practice at the Qatar Grand Prix.

Italian Antonelli was 0.127 seconds quicker than Russell on the medium tyre, as neither driver set a time on the soft compound because of two red flags that punctuated the session.

Lewis Hamilton also came to halt after his Ferrari lost power, with a virtual safety car deployed so the marshals could come to the seven-time world champion's aid.

The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri plus Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the top five at the Lusail International Circuit, with the trio setting soft-tyre times that were more than four tenths adrift of the two Mercedes.

The first red flag was to clear gravel off the track after an incident for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc early on, while the other was to recover the Alpine of Pierre Gasly following a high-speed spin.

Frenchman Gasly hit a marker board before beaching himself after taking too much kerb at Turn 14 in the middle of the qualifying simulation runs.

The interruptions led to the second hour being extended by 13 minutes to allow drivers more time on track in the representative conditions.

"It was a productive day," said Antonelli. "We tried a lot of things on the car between FP1 and FP2, but in FP2, it seemed like we did a step back with the car.

"But it was very interesting to see how the car behaved after those changes. It's not easy."

Antonelli, who secured his maiden title in Mexico City earlier this month, was also fastest in the opening session on the mediums. Mercedes did fit the 20-year-old with the soft tyre in the first hour, but he failed to set a lap time on them.

He said he feels it will be close between himself and Russell for the race victory, but added: "You can never write off Max [Verstappen] and the others."

Norris, meanwhile, said Mercedes "were in a different category" to McLaren, highlighting the Silver Arrows "were quicker in every single corner by miles".

The 2025 world champion added: "We seem in a relatively decent position, similar on pace with Red Bull, and similar-ish to Ferrari. So I'd say it's OK."

Four-time title winner Verstappen said it had been a "difficult day" following his issues with heavy steering towards the end of the session.

"The balance of the car is probably too disconnected at the moment to go fast," he added. "It's costing us quite a bit of lap time."

Hamilton also had a moment with Verstappen that was noted by the race control. The Briton was on a flying lap when he got too close to the Dutchman, who was on a long run.

Verstappen said Hamilton had moved under braking, but the stewards decided no further investigation was needed.

The second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was sixth on the timesheets, with Leclerc leading Hamilton in seventh and eighth, 1.3 seconds away from Antonelli's time.

The two Racing Bulls of British rookie Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson were ninth and 10th.

Leclerc had to head back into the garage after spinning and going through the gravel when Lawson was just ahead of him at Turn Nine.

The Monegasque driver said the car did not feel right, and the Italian team spent a chunk of time repairing the damage to the floor. After the session he said he lost control after going a little bit early on the throttle.

Ferrari arrived in Qatar after another on-track incident between Leclerc and Hamilton, this time in Las Vegas. The pair made contact and Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for the incident, with Hamilton saying on Thursday the team were facing "very, very challenging times".

Leclerc thinks this weekend could potentially be another struggle for the Italian team, who can secure second in the constructors' championship if they can retain at least a 44-point lead over third-placed Red Bull.

"A very, very difficult day. Not even on high fuel were we strong," said Leclerc.

"We are working hard but for some reason, Mercedes is so much faster than I think everyone expected. So the gaps are just a little bit strange."

Drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at the Lusail circuit, meaning teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix on Sunday, which starts at 16:00 GMT.

The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed, 16-corner track. Laps to the grid, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included.

Hamilton was told by his engineer in first practice tyre degradation was "much higher than expected" after highlighting his own issues.

Qatar and next week's finale in Abu Dhabi are going ahead as planned despite the ongoing conflict between the United States/Israel and Iran.

title: 'Bring great bike racing to the people' - Two events debut at USA CRITS for seven races compressed across 22 days in 2027
author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
text:
The Tour of Newport News Criterium and Charlotte Criterium make debuts in the USA CRITS series in 2027, with the compact collection of seven one-day races now spanning 22 days for overall elite rider and team titles, condensing the calendar by a full month.

In its 18th season, with races clustered in four states of the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast regions, the series opener will take place in Newport News, Virginia, on April 10. The finale is set for the High Line Criterium in Suwanee, Georgia, on May 1.

Noticeably absent from the calendar is the Sunny King Criterium, which had been the lead-off event the past three seasons. Anniston has hosted races for state age-group championships as well as collegiate conference championships and organisers will continue to hold two days of racing for a 25th edition April 10-11.

“Nearly 20 years after launching the series, we're still bringing the best riders in the country to communities that embrace the excitement of professional cycling," Gene Dixon, founder of Athens Twilight Criterium and owner of Swagger LLC that produces USA CRITS, said in a press release.

"When we started Athens Twilight in 1980, the idea was simple: bring great bike racing to the people. USA CRITS was built on that same philosophy."

Dixon told that the compact calendar helped simplify travel for riders and teams, especially those traveling from outside the US. While the final set of three races continue to conflict for some teams with Tour of the Gila, April 28-May 2, the earlier finish for the criterium series opens travel for all teams to compete at Tour de Bloom, May 12-16. Also a postivite is that the USA CRITS calendar does not bump into rushed travel to Washington, D.C. for the Amazon Armed Forces Cycling Classic, now early June .

All USA CRITS races will provide live streaming, produced by Swagger. Last year's prize purse totalled $200,000, with equal payouts for elite men and women across individual races and overall series classifications. The USA CRITS D1 Team programme also returns in 2027, with eligible teams provided travel stipends.

The Tour of Newport News is a three-day, five-race event that takes place on the Virginia Peninsula, on the banks of the Hampton Roads harbor near the Atlantic Ocean. USA Cycling-sanctioned events that comprise the omnium include a points race at Todd Stadium, a hill climb up an eight-story parking garage, a time trial and two criteriums. Only the Newport News Twilight Criterium, under the street lights on Saturday night, will set the standings for USA CRITS on Saturday, April 10.

The Charlotte Criterium is a new race that takes place on Friday, April 23, the night before the Winston Salem Cycling Classic. Specifics about the location of the course and start times will be confirmed in the coming months.

title: Garmin's brilliant Varia rearview radar is usually pricey, but you can now grab the RTL515 for less than $150 in this Black Friday deal
author: Paul Norman
text:
A rearview radar has become a must-have accessory for many road cyclists, alerting them to approaching vehicles, how close they are and how fast they're going.

One of the best available is the Garmin RLT515, and this Black Friday it's got 25% off at Backcountry, dropping the price from $200 to just $149.99 for US buyers.

In the UK, Sigma Sports has the RTL515 discounted to £117, down from £169.99; that's a hefty 31% saving.

The market for rearview radars is now quite crowded, but it was Garmin that introduced the category with its first-generation Varia, and it's still arguably the leading brand.

The RTL515 has a claimed detection distance of 140m, although on a straight road in good conditions we reckon it's significantly greater than this. The 220-degree detection angle ensures that vehicles approaching from side roads are detected as well.

The radar links up to a cycling computer , a smartwatch or a phone via Bluetooth or ANT+ and alerts you when a vehicle is detected. It's device-agnostic, so it will work with any brand of cycling computer, not just Garmin.

A fast-approaching vehicle generates a different alert from a slower-moving one, and cycling computers and other devices display how close it is. Once it's passed, there's an all-clear alert.

Four lighting modes include a day flash with 16 hours of claimed battery runtime, a night flash, a constant mode and Peloton mode that lowers the output so that other riders behind you in a group aren't dazzled.

The RTL515 is low in weight at a claimed 71g and is supplied with a robust mount, O-rings to secure it to your seatpost and spacers to suit different seatpost shapes.

REI has a similar 25% Black Friday discount on the Garmin Varia RCT715 , which includes a camera in addition to the tail light and is priced down from $400 to $299.99, while the newer Varia RearVue 820 is priced down from $300 to $249.99.
