title: Mini-pumps begone! The Cycplus AS2 electric inflator is a third off this Black Friday, making it cheaper than many hand pumps
author: Paul Norman
text:
Are the days of the mini pump over? The Cycplus AS2 electric pump is priced down to just $47.49 in the US and £38.95 in the UK on Amazon this Black Friday.

It's the lowest price we've seen for this tiny electric pump and a third off the full retail price that you'd have paid last summer, making it cheaper than many of its competitors and many mini pumps too.

With a claimed weight of just 87g (3oz), it's lighter than most mini pumps. It's smaller too and pocketable, measuring 65 x 44 x 28mm (2.6 x 1.7 x 1.1 inches).

It's supplied with a hose, which you can use to reduce the risk of melting the valve on a TPU inner tube, although it can be directly hooked up to your valve if you're running tubeless or have a less delicate tube to inflate.

We've spent too many hours standing by the road pumping up tubes not to be impressed by the Cycplus pump's around a minute to inflate a tyre to 50psi and it should manage two tyres on a charge.

It's had a battery upgrade since launch too, upping the capacity from 300mAh to 400mAh, which Cycplus reckons will get two 25mm tyres to 110psi, if you like a firm ride. An LED indicator changes from green to amber to red as charge drops.

Plug it into a USB-C charger and it will recharge in a claimed time of just 25 minutes. It comes with the necessary USB-C cable, a range of adapters and a silicone protective sleeve, plus a water resistant ziplock pouch.

If you want to check that your tyre is really up to 110psi before setting off, the Cycplus AS2 Pro has a digital pressure gauge built in. It's a little larger and heavier, but will still fit in a jersey pocket with space to space.

title: World Cup Ostrava: Marie Schreiber cruises to first round elite women's victory on snow-packed course in Czech Republic
author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
text:
After the disappointment of being relegated at the European Championships, Marie Schreiber (SD Worx-Protime) bounced back with a triumph at the first UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup of the season in Ostrava, Czech Republic.

The Luxembourg rider took a solo win in snowy conditions, ahead of runner-up Aniek van Alphen (777 CX Team) and third-placed Manon Bakker. Zoe Bäckstedt (Canyon-SRAM) took fourth, while Ceylin del Carmen Alvarado (Fenix-Premier Tech) was forced to settle for fifth after a crash with two laps to go.

After a slow start and what appeared to be pedal issues, world champion Lucinda Brand (Baloise Verzekeringen-Het Poetsbureu Lions) finished 15th at 2:25 behind the day’s winner and new World Cup leader, Schreiber.

“This was special. It was really nice and something completely new. Yeah, I’ve done one snowy race before but it was a new course, an evening race, it was snowy and cold, and the crowds were amazing, so it was really special. It was awesome,” Schreiber said in a post-race interview to broadcasters.

“At the first part, I had some problems with me pedals, like everyone did, it was really hard to clip in, but then I changed bikes and it was better. Like last week, I needed 20 minutes to get into the race ... but I just settled into a rhythm and try not to make mistakes.

"I couldn’t go all out but had to go with the flow and be really smooth. I managed well, and once I caught Aniek, I could see on some parts I was stronger, I played it smart on the last lap and luckily it worked out.”

The cyclo-cross stars lined up for the opening round of the UCI World Cup under snowy conditions, facing deep ruts along the circuit in Ostrava.

Although Puck Pieterse (Fenix-Premier Tech) was missing from the start, the field was stacked with the likes of world champion Brand, Sara Casasola (Crelan-Corendon) and Fem van Empel (Specialized TMRW), all among the favourites for the night-time cyclo-cross race.

Also on the start line was Shirin van Anrooij, who will have to start the races in a neutral kit for the first five weeks of the cyclo-cross season under UCI regulations, until January 1, when she can wear the kit of her new team, Canyon-SRAM.

A slow start for Brand and Casasola saw the pair racing much further back on the opening circuit than expected, as van Alphen immediately took the lead.

After the first lap, Van Alphen was followed by Alvarado and Schreiber in her wake. She continued her dominance, distancing her rivals and holding an eight-second advantage on the fourth of seven laps ahead of a chasing Schreiber and Bakker. Further back, Alvarado was 22 seconds back, and Kristýna Zemanova (Crelan-Corendon) was 42 seconds.

Although Brand appeared to be gaining time back, moving up to sixth place about 25 seconds back, bad luck struck, and she was forced into the pits for a bike change after a problem with her pedals. She lost significant time, chasing in 22nd place at 1:34 behind the leader.

Bad luck for Alvarado, too, who crashed on the fifth of seven laps, over the handlebars, through the deep snowy ruts, but was up and back on her bike quickly, chasing in fourth place, but with Backstedt close behind.

Under two laps to go, Van Alphen still held a small lead, but with only one second ahead of Schreiber, the pair reconnected as they hit the snow circuit, resetting the race for the victory. The race became even more interesting as Bakker caught the leading duo after a new fastest lap of 7:04, showing strong late-race form.

Schreiber made the winning move on the last lap, opening a small gap to Bakker and Van Alphen, who appeared to struggle to clip in to her pedals.

They were no match for Schreiber, who crossed the line for the win, with Van Alphen taking second and Bakker third, not only winning the first round but also taking the series lead.

title: Police suspect criminals robbed fans at Manchester gig disrupted by ‘unknown substance’
author: Caroline Davies
text:
Police are working with agencies across Europe after similar incidents occurred at two other Don Toliver concerts

A group of organised criminals are believed to have carried out robberies during Don Toliver’s Manchester concert, where an “unknown substance” was released , police have said, with similar incidents having occurred at another two of the US rapper’s gigs in Europe.

Greater Manchester police said they were working to identify the suspects and the substance involved during the incident at the Co-op Live Arena on Sunday evening.

No arrests have been made but mobile phone and CCTV footage is being reviewed by officers, a police statement said. The force is working with other law enforcement agencies across Europe after similar incidents at two Toliver gigs, which officers believe are “relevant” to their inquiries.

Eighty-nine people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure to the substance during the performance in Manchester . The venue was evacuated and a major incident declared as those in the crowd described a “horrible smell”, which police initially believed to be teargas.

Footage shared on social media appeared to show concertgoers coughing and covering their mouths as they left the venue, and medical officials urged anyone who had become unwell after leaving to get in touch. Some of the dozens assessed by doctors reported eye and respiratory symptoms.

Tom Harding, Greater Manchester police assistant chief constable, said: “We’re working to identify those suspects and the substance that we believe was released in the crowd as part of these incidents. All of this work is ongoing at pace.

“There are similar incidents at two Don Toliver gigs in Europe that are also relevant to our inquiries. We’re in contact with law enforcement involved in those investigations.

“No arrests have been made, but our detectives are working through footage captured on mobile phones and CCTV. There are over a 100 people at the gig we are working to try to contact to assist with our inquiries. We thank all those that have assisted us so far.”

Harding said the force was aware some people had been affected psychologically during the Co-op Live incident because of the 2017 terror attack at the Manchester Arena where 22 people were killed by the suicide-bomber Salman Abedi.

He added: “We also know many more people were impacted on the night and afterwards, physically and psychologically. What happened on Sunday night and the imagery on our TVs and online will bring back painful memories of 2017.

“Thankfully, we are not dealing with an incident of such a devastating nature or motive; however, we understand the impact this is likely to have caused.”

title: Antonelli tops Qatar FP2 after multiple red flag delays
author: Samarth Kanal
text:
Kimi Antonelli led Mercedes team-mate George Russell again on Friday as two red flags flew in an extended Formula 1 FP2 session in Qatar.

Antonelli set the benchmark of 1m23.077s on medium tyres before a red flag was flown midway through FP2 for gravel and debris from an early spin for Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc.

Shortly after the session resumed, Alpine’s Pierre Gasly beached his car in the gravel to bring out the second red flag. Late on in FP2, the session was extended by 13 minutes.

Russell was 0.127s off his team-mate with neither Mercedes driver improving on soft tyres as they were both interrupted by stoppages. Antonelli had however set the fastest first sector on softs before the second red flags flew.

McLaren pair Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri were third and fourth respectively, and around 0.45s off the leading Mercedes. They lined up ahead of Red Bull duo Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar who were half a second off Antonelli’s leading pace.

Half a second behind Hadjar was Leclerc in seventh, with his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton in eighth. Hamilton cut across Verstappen late in the session but the stewards deemed no further investigation was necessary.

The seven-time champion stopped off track with four minutes remaining, triggering a virtual safety car, as his Ferrari lost power.

Racing Bulls completed the top 10 with Liam Lawson ninth and 0.1s ahead of team-mate Arvid Lindblad.

Alpine’s Gasly - whose progress was halted by that trip into the gravel - finished between the Audis of Gabriel Bortoleto in 11th and Nico Hulkenberg in 13th.

Williams' Alex Albon was 14th and team-mate Carlos Sainz was 16th, as they were split by Franco Colapinto in the second Alpine.

Rafael Camara was 17th and ahead of Ollie Bearman as Haas eclipsed the Aston Martins and Cadillac rounded out the standings.

Harold Tejada Charged in Doping Case, Netcompany-Ineos Move Collapses Before It Begins
author: ahood
text:
Tejada was provisionally suspended Friday by the ITA. (Photo: Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP via Getty Images)

Netcompany-Ineos is dropping a transfer of Harold Tejada for 2027 after the International Testing Agency charged the Colombian climber with an anti-doping rule violation and provisionally suspended him.

The ITA said Friday it charged Tejada, 29, with using a prohibited substance or method after unexplained abnormalities in the blood values tracked by his Athlete Biological Passport .

An expert panel reviewed Tejada’s explanation and maintained that the abnormalities were “highly likely to have been caused by the administration of a prohibited substance and/or a prohibited method,” the agency said .

The ITA did not identify a specific substance or method, or disclose the dates of the passport data.

The agency imposed a mandatory provisional suspension under UCI rules. Tejada can challenge the suspension and request a hearing before the UCI Anti-Doping Tribunal.

Tejada said on Instagram that the ITA notified him on November 26. He said he had provided the information requested and that his legal and medical team would present his defense.

“I want to clarify that this suspension is a temporary measure and does not constitute a sanction or a final decision,” Tejada wrote . ( See full statement below ).

Netcompany-Ineos announced last month that Tejada would join the British squad for 2027, but the team posted a short message on X announcing that the deal is over.

“Netcompany INEOS and Harold Tejada have agreed to end their agreement for the 2027 season, before he was due to join the team on 1 January,” a note read.

Tejada has raced for XDS-Astana since 2020 and enjoyed a breakout 2026.

He won stage 6 of Paris-Nice, finished fourth overall at the UAE Tour, and hit 10th overall at the Vuelta a España. He also finished second on stage 13 of the Tour de France in Belfort won by Mauro Schmidt.

There was no immediate comment from XDS-Astana officials on Friday.

It’s the latest biological passport case to hit the men’s WorldTour since Oier Lazkano , who was provisionally suspended on October 31, 2025. That case remains unresolved.

To the public, cycling fans and everyone who has supported me throughout my career,

On November 26, 2026, the International Testing Agency (ITA), acting on behalf of the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI), notified me that it had opened anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against me.

I am provisionally suspended pending the outcome of these proceedings in connection with an investigation into my biological passport.

I want to clarify that this suspension is a temporary measure and does not constitute a sanction or a final decision.

From day one, I have acted diligently and responsibly, promptly providing all the information requested of me. I will continue to do so throughout the process, with full respect for the anti-doping authorities and cycling’s governing institutions.

My legal and medical team will present my defense to the relevant bodies through the established channels.

Out of respect for the confidentiality of the proceedings, I will refrain from making any further statements while the case is ongoing.

I am deeply grateful to my family, my friends and everyone who has expressed their support over the past few days.

I respectfully ask for your understanding at this time and for you to respect our privacy.

title: The Guardian view on AI and the Riemann hypothesis: a triumph of intelligence, a test of democracy | Editorial
author: Editorial
text:
Machines are solving problems that have been beyond the reach of human ingenuity. Their growing power must not become the sole preserve of billionaires

For the average person, the news that AI has helped crack a problem that has defied mathematicians since 1859 might elicit momentary awe. What ought to worry everyone is not the discovery per se, but what it says about the power of the machines making it. The pace of scientific discovery looks like it is outrunning the ability of humanity – and its institutions – to understand, let alone regulate, AI’s advances.

Last Friday Levent Alpöge , a mathematician at Anthropic, said that he, with the assistance of an unreleased version of the company’s Claude chatbot, had produced what many mathematicians see as the holy grail: a proof for the Riemann hypothesis . Mathematicians like Cornell University’s Steven Strogatz had already cried on podcasts, lamenting that students were asking: “What’s the point if the AI can do math better than any human being?” Computers can validate the Alpöge-Claude proof. But Prof Strogatz fears AI’s discoveries may soon defy human understanding. Asking AI to explain them, he said, would be like him trying to teach calculus to his own dog.

title: Percy Jackson, the Helm of Hades, and Annabeth Chase’s Yankees hat
author: John Griffin
text:
A Yankee hat plays an important role in the Disney+ series.

Earlier today, the third and fourth episodes of Percy Jackson and the Olympians season three premiered on Disney+. Adapted from the Rick Riordan books of the same name, the series centers on the titular son of Poseidon as he and his friends grappled with the gods and monsters of the ancient Greeks and Romans, alive and well and living in North America. Two years ago, in the aftermath of the season one finale (and our Top 100 Yankees series here at Pinstripe Alley), I dove into Yankees history, asking the rather amusing question, “ Which legendary Yankees figures were secretly the gods of Mt. Olympus? ”

As the new season of the television show approached, I found myself thinking about another place where Percy Jackson and baseball intersect: Annabeth Chase’s Yankees hat. A gift from her mother, the goddess Athena, the Yankees hat is more than a simple baseball cap, also functioning as a magical item that turns the wearer invisible. For those who know Greek mythology, it is a clear reference to the Helm of Hades (also known variously as the Helm of Darkness, the Cap of Hades, and the Cap of Invisibility), a magical item normally associated with the God of the Underworld but which others use sporadically throughout Greek mythological history.

Within the Percy Jackson universe, items and places from Greek myths are reimagined all the time: Mt. Olympus is in the Empire State Building, Charon the ferryman is an elevator operator, and Apollo’s sun chariot is a sports car. And so I began to wonder, why did the author decide to make a magical item inspired by the Helm (but which is itself not the helm — that specific item appears elsewhere in the story) out of a Yankees hat?

To answer that question, we first need to dive a bit into the mythical helm. While it’s hard to find an ancient depiction of it, here’s how Renaissance and Enlightenment era artists tended to depict it, as seen through this statue of Perseus holding the head of Medusa:

Sure, this doesn’t help us understand what the ancient one looked like (that’s a bit harder to determine), but it does show us that… well, it’s not some big special thing, just a normal everyday item that is imbued with magical properties. This, in fact, reflects most things in mythology: modern depictions of Cerberus, the guard dog of Hades, depict him as a big, scary monster, but in antiquity he was just a simple dog that happened to have three heads; see, for example, this statue group of Hades, Persephone, and Cerberus from the first century BCE:

With that in mind, it’s clear that, for a modern day invisibility cap, Riordan was looking not for something extraordinary and noticeable, but rather something incredibly mundane. And in the United States in the 21st century, what headwear is more mundane than a baseball cap? I mean, baseball caps with the logos of basketball, football, hockey, and soccer teams are everywhere. Colleges and high schools plaster their school logo on them. Even the US military and veterans’ organizations employ baseball caps, both as part of certain uniforms and as non-uniform gear. The baseball cap has spread well beyond its original use on the diamond, and has become one of, if not arguably the, American fashion accessory.

So it makes sense why Riordan would make the modern-day cap of invisibility out of a baseball cap. But why, specifically, a Yankees hat? It could simply be narrative convenience — the Percy Jackson series centers on New York, and when people think of baseball hats in New York City, they tend to think of Yankee hats (apologies to any Mets fans reading this, but it’s true). Narrative convenience, though, is not in my mind a sufficient answer, even if it hints at the real answer: the author immediately jumps from baseball cap to Yankee hat because, ultimately, the Yankee hat is the default baseball cap not just in New York, but within public consciousness. Check out, for example, the Wikipedia page for “ baseball cap; ” at the time of writing, the top image on the page, normally designed to give the reader an understanding of the topic, is a Yankee hat. And so, when trying to create the most mundane, unexciting, run-of-the-mill modern hat? Well, in truth, there’s only one option.

title: Labour row over Rosebank deepens as dozens of MPs warn PM not to block oilfield
author: Kiran Stacey and Patrick Greenfield
text:
Warning of ‘lights out for Labour in Scotland’ as Burnham faces choice between warring factions over North Sea drilling project

Dozens of Labour MPs in favour of Rosebank are putting pressure on the prime minister not to block the North Sea oilfield, warning that doing so could spell “lights out for Labour in Scotland”.

As many as 80 pro-drilling MPs are considering writing their own letter to Andy Burnham after nearly 100 of their colleagues called on the prime minister not to allow the project to proceed . Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra has also reiterated his support for Rosebank, cautioning that “working-class people in vocational jobs” were threatened by the decline of the North Sea basin.

Burnham now faces having to choose between two warring factions within his own party in what is likely to be the most sensitive decision he has taken so far as prime minister.

Anti-Rosebank MPs warn about the impact on the climate. They argue that the estimated additional 254m tonnes of carbon dioxide which Rosebank will produce over its lifetime are not worth the extra £500m in tax receipts and 500 jobs it will generate.

But those in favour of the project worry that a decision not to go ahead will damage Labour’s reputation with industry and Scottish voters in general.

One MP told the Guardian: “This is very much part of Scotland’s economy and supply chain, but crucially Scotland’s identity. It has become such a totemic issue that Labour will not be forgiven in Scotland if they don’t do this.”

The person added: “Andy needs to approve Rosebank or it’s lights out for Labour in Scotland.”

Marra said he recognised that the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, had a “different” decision compared to the Jackdaw gasfield , but backed the project because of the jobs and economic activity it would support.

“The decline of the North Sea may be seen as something to celebrate by those who want us to meet our climate obligations.

“I understand that. But I ask those who call for a just transition to understand the anxiety in Aberdeen and the north-east of Scotland over a political establishment which often feels to them that it considers anything but clean energy a dirty word.

“This is people’s lives and livelihoods we are talking about. Not the millionaire shareholders of a billion-dollar multinational, but working-class people in vocational jobs,” the Scottish Labour leader said.

Several MPs have sent individual letters to Burnham urging him to allow the project to go ahead, but many are now in talks about whether to coordinate their efforts to counteract a letter against Rosebank signed by nearly 100 of their collegaues.

One Labour MP said: “The whips and the government know we have the support, we’ve made that clear behind the scenes. Conversations [over a joint letter] are ongoing over the weekend.”

Another added: “Reindustrialisation and energy jobs for young people are huge issues in Scotland, so the feeling is they need to approve it to show we’re serious about it.”

Henry Tufnell, Labour MP for mid and south Pembrokeshire said: “Failing to approve Rosebank would cost industrial communities jobs and investment, weaken our balance of payments and deny the exchequer vital tax revenues.”

Torcuil Crichton, the Labour MP for Na h-Eileanan an Iar (Western Isles), said: “We need the workforce, the supply chain and the expertise of the North Sea to build our renewable future.

“There are now more jobs in renewables than in the carbon sector, but we can’t abandon the workforce like other energy communities were abandoned by the Tories.”

He told BBC Radio Scotland: “It makes far more sense from a domestic security point of view and an environmental point of view to source those carbon fuels within our own boundaries. If we don’t, we’re importing a huge carbon footprint from other places.

“So there’s no point outsourcing our environmental conscience.”

Burnham has enjoyed early success in office by uniting his previously fractious parliamentary party and winning back voters who had defected to other leftwing parties. The Rosebank decision, however, will test his ability to keep his fragile coalitions of MPs and voters together.

While Labour has enjoyed a poll bounce since Burnham became prime minister , the improvement has been more modest in Scotland and the party remains behind the Scottish National party.

In recent months, the SNP’s stance on oil and gas drilling in the North Sea has shifted. Once strong opponents of new projects under Nicola Sturgeon, the party abandoned its “presumption against” new North Sea projects in October. John Swinney has also criticised the UK government’s energy independence bill, which aims to ban new North Sea drilling.

Polling by Survation last month found that 64% of people in Scotland say that the UK government should approve Rosebank, with 16% against.

“In Scotland, the public supports approval for Rosebank in every age group excepted 18-to-24s. But even that is very close: there’s just a 1% net difference. According to our polling, allowing the project to go ahead would make Scottish voters more likely to vote Labour. Any route to a majority for Burnham hinges on Scottish seats,” said PJ Stock, a research and data analyst with Survation.

Emma Hardy, the environment minister, acknowledged on Friday morning that her party was split over the issue.

She told Sky News: “I know from chatting to some of my friends and colleagues, some Labour MPs in Scotland feel differently to some Labour MPs elsewhere. But I know Andy [Burnham], as our prime minister, will be listening to everybody.”

While Labour went into the last election promising not to issue any more North Sea oil and gas licences, they could give the environmental approval to this project – the largest undeveloped field in UK waters – because it already has a licence.…

title: Netcompany Ineos cancel new transfer Harold Tejada before 2027 season amid biological passport anti-doping investigation
author: James Moultrie
text:
Netcompany Ineos have agreed to terminate the agreement with one of their new signings for the 2027 season before his contract even begins on January 1, amid a provisional suspension and investigation into the biological passport of Colombian rider Harold Tejada.

Not even 50 days have passed since Ineos announced Tejada as a new name set to bolster their climbing ranks, but after he revealed on Friday afternoon that he had been notified by the International Testing Agency (ITA) of an anti-doping disciplinary proceeding against him, an announcement from the British team followed an hour later.

"Netcompany INEOS and Harold Tejada have agreed to end their agreement for the 2027 season, before he was due to join the team on 1 January," read a post from the team on X.

A winner of a Paris-Nice stage this season, Tejada was set to be one of nine new transfers already announced for Netcompany Ineos in 2027, as they look to rebuild back to their former GC glory.

Tejada maintains his innocence. His statement highlighted that the suspension is "a temporary measure, which does not constitute a sanction nor a definitive decision", and he confirmed that he will be working with a legal and medical team to "exercise my defense before the relevant bodies, through the established channels."

The ITA released a press release, echoing Tejada's statement, but also confirming that it had charged Tejada with an anti-doping rule violation (ADRV) "for the use of a prohibited substance or a prohibited method based on unexplained abnormalities in his athlete biological passport (ABP)."

"The ITA reports that the ABP¹ of Colombian road cyclist Harold Alfonso Tejada Canacue has returned an Adverse Passport Finding (APF)² due to unexplained abnormalities in the values of his haematological ABP," read the release.

"Specifically, a panel of experts has confirmed that the rider has a case to answer, as, after reviewing the rider’s explanation, the panel maintained that the abnormalities in his ABP are highly likely to have been caused by the administration of a prohibited substance and/or a prohibited method.

"The rider has been informed of the charge and has the right to provide additional information. The rider has the possibility to accept the consequences for his violation or to request for the matter to be referred to the UCI Anti-Doping Tribunal for a hearing.

"Further, in accordance with the UCI anti-doping rules and article 6.2.1 of the UCI regulations for results management (UCI RMR), a mandatory provisional suspension has been imposed on the rider. The rider has the right to challenge the provisional suspension and ask for its lifting."

As listed on the ITA's website: " The ABP is an individual electronic profile that monitors selected biological variables of an athlete. It contains the results of the athletes’ urine and blood samples, which are tracked consistently. Any significant variation from normal levels can be assessed for possible manipulation. At the ITA, ABP management is performed by a specialist unit of experts who liaise with the Athlete Passport Management Units (APMUs) and ABP Expert Panels in order to issue further targeted testing or in case of adverse or atypical findings."

Tejada's statement in full

"To the general public, cycling fans, and everyone who has accompanied me throughout my career: on November 26, 2026, I was notified by the International Testing Agency (ITA), on behalf of the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI), of the initiation of an anti-doping disciplinary proceeding against me.

"While this proceeding is being resolved, I am provisionally suspended in relation to an investigation into my biological passport.

"I want to clarify that this suspension is a temporary measure, which does not constitute a sanction or a final decision.

"From day one, I have acted with diligence and responsibility, providing all requested information in a timely manner. I will continue to do so throughout the entire process, with full respect for the anti-doping authorities and cycling institutions.

"My legal and medical team will work to exercise my defense before the relevant bodies, through the established channels.

"In consideration of the confidentiality of the proceeding, I will refrain from making additional statements while the case is ongoing.

"I deeply thank my family, my friends, and all the people who have expressed their support to me during these days. I ask you, with all due respect, to understand this moment and respect our privacy.

"Harold Alfonso Tejada Canacue"

author: Michael Zeno
text:
An exceptional fourth quarter on Wednesday made a fourth consecutive trip to the NBA Cup knockout round a possibility.

After the Knicks’ valiant comeback effort at Gainbridge Fieldhouse came up empty on November 13, they fell to 6-6 on the season and 0-2 in NBA Cup play. After an incredible run the year prior to claim the organization’s first trophy of any kind in 27 years (foreshadowing), they seemed fated to become the third consecutive NBA Cup champion to be bounced in the group stage.

Yet, one six-game winning streak and an incredible fourth quarter in a Cup game against the Cavs later, and the Knicks are mathematically alive heading into Black Friday against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the red-hot Miami Heat.

Now, after winning the Treble last year, experiencing the fatigue from last year’s Cup run that led to the 2-9 stretch from hell, and, you know, defending a real championship, a tournament that already had limited interest from Knicks fans seems to have the opposite intended effect, to the point where it might be beneficial to miss the knockout round altogether.

But the Knicks are currently the only team to have never been grouped in Cup play, and since these games count toward the team’s 82-game record, there’s plenty to play for as the Knicks look to defend the first of their three trophies.

Here’s a look at the current standings in East Group B and the East’s wild card, both of which are still in play:

The simplest path is to win the group, which simply requires two things:

What helps the Knicks here is their point differential. They lost the games to Philly and Indiana by five and two points respectively, which allowed their 19-point win over Cleveland to put them in a decent spot.

Winning an NBA game by seven is the easy part; relying on an injured and struggling Pacers team to defeat the No. 1 seed in the East is another. Now, the Sixers look like a paper tiger with their clutch reliance (their Cup PD is negative because of this), but this reads like a game that would be a blowout.

The current injury report has Jaylen Brown out with hamstring management and Joel Embiid questionable with an illness for the Sixers, while Tyrese Haliburton, Ben Sheppard, and Johnny Furphy are still out for Indiana. TJ McConnell, Larry Nance Jr., and Kelly Oubre Jr. are questionable.

If the Sixers win, they clinch Group B. If they lose, the Knicks will get a shot at being the first 2-loss NBA Cup group winner in an unlikely five-way tie.

In the event of a Sixers win, things get a lot more complicated.

First of all, the Knicks would need there to be zero 3-1 non-group winners for obvious reasons. That means they’ll need losses from the Hawks, Pistons, and Raptors. Toronto already has a lower point differential, so margin wouldn’t matter there.

Margin would matter with the other two. The Hawks are at +21 and the Pistons are at +31, so the Knicks are going to need to win and win by a lot to guarantee they get in.

The simplest path to a wild card berth in the event of a Sixers win looks like this:

The margin of victory would likely not need to be that big, as the more the Pistons and Hawks lose by, the more it knocks that down. The absolute minimum the Knicks would have to win by is seven to pass the Heat in point differential, but to only have to win by that much, they’d need the Bucks to win by 13 and the Celtics to win by 3.

Which brings the difficulty aspect. You’re asking two of the worst teams in the league to win games against significantly better teams, one of which is a matchup between a 2-win Bucks team and the reigning No. 1 seed. That’s probably not happening.

Also, there is the spoiler aspect that could theoretically damage both of these scenarios. If the Pacers (-27 PD) or Nets (-11 PD) win by such ridiculous margins, they would have a chance to steal a spot in the knockout round.

Now, personally, a Hali-less Pacers team winning by damn near 50 or the Nets beating the Raptors by 30+ would be pretty stunning, but we’re already asking for stunning things to happen to get this far.

In layman’s terms, a fourth consecutive trip to the knockout round is still unlikely, but possible.

It’ll make for a fun night of scoreboard watching, that’s for sure.

title: 50-year-old structure led Williams to F1 cost cap breach
author: Josh Suttill
text:
Williams has explained that overdue company restructuring triggered its Formula 1 cost cap penalty, as it made changes it thought were excluded from the cost cap.

The team was found to have breached the 2025 cost cap by £627,000 (0.48% of the total cap) and will have to pay the FIA a financial penalty - as well as lose 1.5% of its windtunnel and CFD testing time for the next 12 months.

Team boss James Vowles faced a number of questions on the breach during the Friday press conference in Qatar.

“The background to it is that the company structure of Williams was largely unchanged from 1977 and wasn't really fit for purpose in a modern world,” Vowles said.

“We went into it with every intention of being open, transparent with the FIA, which is what we held all the way throughout, but believed those costs, because it's company restructuring, [would] not be a cost cap expense.

“It was the company restructuring that put us over. We’ve had no financial benefit from it, no sporting benefit as a result of it, and you can see that the penalty is pretty much adjusted to be in line with that as well at the same time.

“But it was our interpretation of that, is that those costs are out of cap. The FIA’s interpretation of it are that they are in cap, and obviously we went with the FIA’s interpretation after much discussion.”

Vowles called it a “one-off company restructuring” because the previous structure “wasn't quite fit for purpose”.

Vowles encouraged “those interested” to look at Williams’s accounts on Companies House.

According to Companies House, during 2025 the team “transferred much of its trade and assets to a newly formed subsidiary, Williams Grand Prix Engineering Services LLP, an entity in which the company is a 99% member.

“This update to the corporate structure makes the organisation fit for the future, having been relatively unchanged in the nearly 50 years of operation since formation,

“The changes are about future-proofing our business, enabling smarter ways of working and positioning us to stay competitive at the highest level.

“The inclusion of a partner group will aid retention of certain staff and recognises the importance of those people to the delivery of the business plan.

“Member distributions have been declared to the 1% member of Williams Grand Prix Engineering Services LLP.”

Vowles described it as “Fundamentally, it's a single vertical structure as what was there previously.

“There's many downsides to fundamentally having that. You'll see there's a number of other companies have been created around it, which is just more efficient.

“The costs involved in it are fairly significant. If you think about what you have to do as a business, you probably have, in our case, close to 2,000 contracts with various suppliers and otherwise, that you have to migrate from one company to the next as a result of it. It's a very painful, lengthy task.

“There's some legal that goes with it. There's some compliance you have to do in UK law as a result of it as well at the same time.

“It was a process in the end that took, we initiated it probably around about six months, which probably gives you an idea as to how lengthy it is.

“But it was using finance and legal personnel for that period of which we had to bolster up to get us through that period.”

Williams fell down because it had a different interpretation of the regulations to the FIA.

“Clearly, we should have done something differently as a result of it,” Vowles admitted.

“Although the regulations aren't clear and black and white, it's interpretation, but the FIA is very clear on their perspective, which is the following: Because you've moved contracts from one business to the next, that effectively for them is procurement, which is an included activity.

“For us, we defined it as a financial and legal activity because it's literally taking a contract and changing a name on it.

“I can understand their interpretation, which is why we've accepted the breach, but I hope that helps you understand why it's subtleties, not clarity, really, in that circumstance.”

Vowles isn’t too worried about that 1.5% reduction in windtunnel and CFD testing time given that under the Aerodynamic Testing Restrictions system, there’s a sliding scale of windtunnel and CFD time in 5% increments.

“I think to put things in perspective, one position on the grid is 5% of ATR, and we've got a 1.5% delta. So it's less than a third of a position,” Vowles said.

“I'm rather hoping that we do a better job next year and put ourselves back up the grid, and that would be 15% something in that ballpark.

“So the reality is it's going to be small beans in the grand scheme of things.”

Williams is currently ninth out of 11 teams as of the last ATR period, and that’s unlikely to change for the start of 2027. That table will then reset after the first ATR period ends halfway through 2027 - when by Vowles’s 15% ballpark estimation, Williams will hope to be around sixth in the championship.

title: Mark Cavendish’s former coach joins Ben Swift among the staff reinforcements at Netcompany Ineos
author: Owen Rogers
text:
British WorldTour team Netcompany Ineos have announced three new additions to their support staff, with the recently-retired Ben Swift , Vasilis Anastopoulos and Professor Asker Jeukendrup joining in the team’s backroom.

As expected, after a 19-year career as a rider which included 15 race victories and two podium finishes in Milan-Sanremo, Swift will take up a role as one of the team’s sports directors. Having switched from a sprinter and Classics rider to a role as a road captain in recent years, he should be able to develop those leadership skills in his new role.

"I know how much the people around a rider matter, because I've been that rider," Swift said in a team press release. "I'll miss racing, no doubt. But I'm excited to give something back from the car, keep learning, and bring the same commitment I had as a rider."

Anastopoulos, also a former professional rider, is perhaps best known as the coach who oversaw Mark Cavendish’s return to winning form during the sprinter’s second spell with Soudal-QuickStep. He then went with Cavendish when he moved to the Astana team, and guided the sprinter to his 35th and record-breaking Tour de France stage win .

He joins Netcompany from the Kazakh team, where he’s been head of performance since 2023, and will join the team’s coaching staff in a "senior role".

Finally, Prof. Jeukendrup joins the team as director of physiology and nutrition after a career working in high performance sport, including across multiple sports as performance manager with the Dutch TeamNL and two years as director of sport strategy at Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, a role he left last month.

It’s been a busy week for Netcompany Ineos, who first announced that former Tour de France and Giro d’Italia winner Egan Bernal extended his contract, apparently until the end of 2029. Then, hours after that announcement, they revealed seven other current riders were staying with the British outfit, with Connor Swift, Ben Swift’s cousin, committing until the end of the 2029 season as well.

title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
text:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights

Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.

In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning , the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.

“Bill 21 is rooted in Quebec’s legitimate and historical commitment to ensuring the laicity of the state in a free and democratic society,” chief justice Richard Wagner wrote in the majority opinion.

Canada’s top court says the four days of hearings from earlier in the year marked one of the longest in its 151-year history. Fifty-one interveners participated, including six attorneys general – also a record number. The court’s website crashed on Friday morning when the judgment was released.

While the judgment was celebrated by some in Quebec who considered it a vindication of the province’s fight, it was swiftly criticised by religious civil liberties groups.

“We cannot exist in a country as free people, where governments can literally go to the electorate and say, ‘I’m gonna take away the rights of a certain group of minorities’, because it’s popular and to play wedge politics with the charter rights of Canadians,” Stephen Brown, chief executive of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, told reporters at a press conference. “If that is the case, we don’t have a charter of rights and freedoms. We have a charter of suggestions and permissions.”

Passed in 2019, Quebec’s secularism law, Bill 21, bars workers including lawyers, judges, police and teachers from wearing religious symbols such as a hijab, turban, kippah or a cross while on the job.

Central to the case – and the reason provincial governments across the country are closely watching the result – is the “notwithstanding clause”, a constitutional mechanism that allows elected governments to override certain fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed by Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

The clause is the result of political compromise from the 1980s, when the federal government set out to replace the existing British North America Act with a new constitution. Provinces feared that under a new constitution, courts would become too powerful, undermining the authority of the elected government. A compromise was hashed out: in cases when a government – provincial or federal – felt that the courts had overstepped, they could invoke the clause to override certain charter rights of citizens.

Some fundamental rights, including protections of religious freedom, equality and speech, could be suspended. But voting, as well as language rights, were untouchable, ensuring Canadians could remove a government if they wanted. A government could only invoke the clause for five years. Before they could renew it, they would first have to face voters .

In its decision, the supreme court rejected most arguments that Bill 21 violated portions of the charter that are not subject to the notwithstanding clause, including guarantees relating to the equality of men and women and the education rights of Quebec’s English-speaking minority.

Quebec’s use of the clause with Bill 21 was notable – and controversial – in that it was the first time the notwithstanding clause had been invoked pre-emptively in an attempt to shield the law from court challenges. Quebec also passed Bill 96 , which sought to strengthen French language protections – again pre-emptively invoking the notwithstanding clause.

But groups affected by those laws can still challenge them and many teachers, religious and civil liberties groups argued it was a clear violation of constitutional rights and reflected government overreach. Quebec’s government has defended the law, saying it is constitutionally valid.

In April 2021, a Quebec superior court judge described the effects of the law as “cruel”, saying it “dehumanises” the people it targets, but conceded the statute could not be struck down because it was protected by the notwithstanding clause. Quebec’s court of appeal also upheld the law in February 2024 on the same grounds.

In its 520-page judgment, the court did find that element of the law infringed on democratic rights protected by the charter, including preventing elected members of Quebec’s National Assembly who wear face coverings for religious reasons from participating in the legislative process.

In a 4-3 decision, the court also endorsed the ability of lower courts to issue “judicial declarations” on laws protected by the notwithstanding clause, giving judges the power to declare a law in violation of the charter, even though the law would be permitted to stand.

The court’s decision was celebrated in Quebec, where the governing Parti Québécois has looked for wedges with the federal government and institutions like the supreme court.

The premier, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, had previously said his province’s right to decide its own laws was at risk.

Canada only recently fended off a threat to national unity after voters in Alberta rejected the initial stages of a separatist push. But Quebec’s newly elected government has shown an eagerness to clash with the prime minister, Mark Carney.

The supreme court’s judgment comes on the same day an appeal will be heard regarding a superior court decision that forces Quebec’s members of the national assembly to swear allegiance to King Charles to sit in the Salon Bleu – the chamber of the assembly. Lawmakers from a number of parties in the province recently refused to swear the oath of allegiance.

title: Forget Pauline Ferrand-Prévot. She’s Pauline van Baarle Now.
author: Jim Cotton
text:
(Photo: Francois LO PRESTI / AFP via Getty Images)

Pauline Ferrand-Prévot is taking a new name now that she’s married Dylan van Baarle .

And thankfully, it’s not “Pauline Ferrand-Prévot van Baarle.”

“I would like to be called Pauline van Baarle,” the 34-year-old superstar told NOS on Friday.

The rider who was “PFP” married fellow pro cyclist “DVB” last month in the Netherlands.

This first-ever marriage of two Paris-Roubaix champions marked the end of an era.

Pauline told NOS on Friday that her home French fans will have to suck up the loss of their affectionate PFP moniker and start practicing their pronunciation.

“I understand that it won’t be easy for everyone to pronounce, but for me and for Dylan, it is very important,” she said.

“I will be a little more Dutch next year,” she joked.

It’s all change for Pauline van Baarle next year.

The revelation of her new name came the very same day her team also took a new married identity.

The women’s team that was Visma-Lease a Bike became Rabobank-Lease a Bike on Friday after the Dutch bank stepped up to take co-title sponsorship of the squad.

Beyond that, PVB might be approaching the bike a little differently in 2027.

She explained in an Instagram post celebrating her wedding earlier this month that she’d endured a long period of self-reflection after she burned herself out preparing for her Tour de France Femmes title defense.

“It was an absolutely special day,” she wrote about her wedding. “I remembered being happy when winning the Olympics, Tour, or Roubaix. But this feeling of getting married to Dylan with the presence of the most important people in my life was another level of joy, happiness, and fulfillment.

“Experiencing this feeling of being so happy while not sacrificing everything or being extreme was something I never experienced before. On that last sentence I will take note for the future,” she wrote.

Au revoir , Tour de France-obsessed Pauline Ferrand-Prévot.

Hallo to the wedded, wiser Pauline van Baarle.

title: Yankee Birthday of the Day: Bullet Joe Bush
author: Matt Ferenchick
text:
A good chunk of the heroes from Yankees history are one-team players who spent their entire careers in the Bronx. I’m talking Lou Gehrig, Joe DiMaggio, and Mickey Mantle to modern ones like Derek Jeter and Aaron Judge.

However, it’s somewhat well known that the first couple decades in franchise history weren’t very successful. When the Yankees did finally reach the mountain top in 1923, the roster — including Babe Ruth — had a lot of key players who had notable runs elsewhere that had been acquired through trades.

One of that list includes Bullet Joe Bush, who would be celebrating a birthday today.

Leslie Ambrose “Bullet Joe” Bush November 27, 1892 (Ehime, MN) November 1, 1974 (Fort Lauderdale, FL) 1922-24

Bush was born in Minnesota in 1892, one of seven children. He was dubbed “Joe” as a child, although the Bullet part of his nickname wasn’t added until his baseball career, as you might expect. As a child, Bush was said to practice his pitching by throwing “rotten apples through a crescent-shaped hole of a neighboring outhouse.”

He began playing more organized baseball for the Brainerd, MN town team when he was 13 years old. Originally, Bush played third base. However, he was converted to a pitcher after the team captain noticed the speed at which his throws came in at. That’s when he truly began to get noticed, and a Montana-based minor league team eventually signed him when Bush was 18.

In Montana, Bush’s manager was Cliff Blankenship, who had been credited for discovering Hall of Fame pitcher Walter Johnson. Blankenship mentored Bush before recommending him to Philadelphia Athletics’ manager Connie Mack. The A’s legend took his advice, and Bush was soon making his MLB debut as a 19-year old in August 1912.

In 1913, A’s ace Jack Coombs missed most of the season with an illness, which led to Bush getting a more prominent role for the team. His numbers on the whole weren’t spectacular, but he went 15-6 for Philadelphia as they won the AL pennant. In the World Series, Bush was entrusted to start Game 3, and allowed just two runs (one earned) in a complete game victory over the Giants. The series was tied going into Game 3 and Philadelphia rode that win to take the series in five.

After that season, Bush became a fixture in the A’s rotation. It took until 1916 for his rate stats like ERA to become genuinely good, but he did help Philadelphia make it back to the World Series in 1914, although they were swept by the Braves.

However, as Bush began to become an excellent pitcher, the A’s team began to become way less than excellent. With the introduction of the rebel Federal League, Mack began to sell away players from that 1913 World Series-winning team rather than get into bidding wars, including Home Run Baker to the Yankees. It was hardly all his fault, but Bush ended up suffering a league-leading 24 losses in 1916.

Eventually, Bush became part of the A’s sell-off and he was sent to the Red Sox in December 1917. In Boston, Bush immediately turned in one his best seasons to date in 1918, helping the Red Sox to the World Series. Boston ended up beating the Cubs in six games in the series. Bush lost his only start in Game 2, but he came out of the bullpen in Game 4. A still-pitching Babe Ruth was nursing a one-run lead going into the ninth but allowed the first two runners to reach. Bush came in and got a bunt force out at third and a double play to seal a 3-2 win. That gave Boston a crucial 3-1 lead in the series.

An arm injury forced Bush to miss almost all of the 1919 season, but he came back in 1920 armed with a new weapon. During his return from injury, Bush stumbled across the forkball, which he is credited with inventing. While he was only okay in 1920, by 1921 he had mastered the pitch and was back to his best.

However once again, financial concerns soon led to the breakup of a World Series-winning team Bush was on. Red Sox owner Harry Frazee began selling off players from that 1918 team. Many of those deals saw Red Sox stars going to the Yankees, most notably Ruth. Bush eventually became part of that list as he, fellow pitcher Sad Sam Jones , and shortstop Everett Scott were traded to New York in December 1921.

UNSPECIFIED – UNDATED: New York Yankees’ Joe Bush. (Photo by Pacific & Atlantic/Sports Studio Photos/Getty Images)

| Getty Images" data-portal-copyright="Getty Images"> Once again though, Bush joined a team on the brink of success. Thanks in part to Bush’s 26 wins, the Yankees won the AL pennant in 1922, although they fell to the Giants in the World Series. However the following year, Bush pitched a team-high 275.2 innings, helping the team back to the World Series. This time they emerged victorious, besting the Giants in six games. Bush himself got dinged with a loss in Game 1 despite allowing only one run in 6.2 innings out of the bullpen. In Game 5, he again came up big in the Fall Classic, allowing just one run in a complete game, giving the Yankees a 3-2 lead in the series. They clinched the franchise’s first championship the following day.

Bush had a down season in 1924 as the Yankees failed to make it back to the World Series. The team opted to trade him to the St. Louis Browns for fellow pitcher Urban Shocker . Bush became a bit of a journeyman after that, playing for several teams before ending his MLB career back with the A’s in 1928.

After a couple more years playing in the minors, Bush transitioned to coaching and led the Allentown Buffaloes to the Eastern League pennant in 1930. After leaving baseball, Bush held a variety of jobs before retiring to Florida, where he lived until passing away in 1974.

Bullet Joe Bush is one of just two dozen or so players to have won a World Series championship with three different teams. He also came up remarkably big in all of those championships too.

See more of the “Yankees Birthday of the Day” series here .

title: British Gas owner seeks urgent government talks over future of storage facility
author: Jillian Ambrose
text:
Centrica boss memo to 400 workers at gas plant off Yorkshire coast says utility doing all it can ‘to save your jobs’

The boss of the British Gas owner Centrica has told hundreds of staff at its largest gas storage facility that he was seeking urgent talks with Andy Burnham and would do everything he could to save jobs.

Chris O’Shea, the chief executive of Centrica, reportedly told staff at the Rough gas storage facility off the east Yorkshire that the government had rebuffed the company’s plea for short-term support to run the store over the winter.

In a memo, seen by Sky News, O’Shea is understood to have expressed disappointment that the government had delayed its response to a consultation on whether to support the ageing underground gas stores over the longer term.

The Guardian understands that the government delivered its decision to Centrica in the last few weeks and the internal company memo was intended to update the facility’s staff about continuing talks.

The Rough gas storage facility supports about 400 jobs, including direct employees and contractors, but is scheduled to close at the end of March – unless the government intervenes – because it has become uneconomic to run.

Facilities typically store gas in the summer when the market price is lower, and sell it in winter when the price rises due to higher demand. But successive energy crises in recent years have upended this pattern, making it difficult to make enough money to invest in the upgrade work needed to keep the facility running.

“No decisions about roles have been made,” O’Shea wrote in the memo, according to Sky News. He reportedly added that the company was “doing everything we can to save your jobs” and that he would seek urgent talks with trade unions, Whitehall officials and the prime minister on the issue.

It is the latest in a series of warnings by Centrica over the future of the site. Centrica is listed on the FTSE 100, valued at nearly £7bn.

The jobs warning has emerged less than a fortnight after the energy company SSE told investors it would shut its Atwick gas storage site in east Yorkshire next summer unless the government offered support.

SSE said although the site continued to have “strategic importance” to the energy system as the North Sea’s domestic production declined, it was “increasingly clear” that the market would not support its continued operations.

Earlier this month, the National Energy System Operator (Neso) used a second consecutive annual report to warn that the UK was at risk of a gas supply crisis as the North Sea’s production wound down.

The report underlined concerns raised in Neso’s first annual report which found that while the UK has enough access to global gas markets to cover demand when weather is normal, if even a single piece of Britain’s ageing gas infrastructure suffered an “unlikely” outage during a very cold spell, then the UK could run out of gas.

A spokesperson for Centrica declined to comment.

title: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights
author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
text:
Norwegian airline tells customers not to come to airports after surging fuel costs caused by Iran war ruin finances

Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights after surging fuel costs caused by the Iran war ruined its finances.

The Norwegian airline said it was entering insolvency and posted a message on its website telling customers not to come to airports – including passengers stranded away from home. Its collapse came a day after it put flights on hold with a warning that its finances were critical.

The carrier operated low-cost, long-haul flights around the world, including from London Gatwick and the US to Europe and Asia. Flights from Gatwick and Manchester next month to Thailand are among those now scrapped, along with London flights to South Africa and the US.

The Norse board concluded operations were no longer viable after a year in which airlines across the world were hit by spiralling oil prices that doubled the cost of jet fuel as well as dampening consumer demand, after the Iran war began in February.

Rival airlines have predicted surging air fares and the collapse of weaker carriers .

In a statement to the Oslo stock exchange, Eivind Roald, the chief executive of Norse, said: “The board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has made the difficult decision to file for bankruptcy despite extensive efforts from the company and the group to find a solution.

“We are deeply sorry for the impact this has on our passengers, employees and partners.”

He said the owning group and Norse’s UK subsidiary – which was set up to comply with aviation rules after Brexit – were “working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations”.

However, all UK flights were similarly cancelled and ticket sales halted.

In a message on its website, Norse advised passengers to contact their travel agents, flight bookers, insurers or credit card companies, but made clear those travelling were on their own and should ask airport information desks.

It said: “We know this will disrupt travel plans and may leave some passengers away from home. Customer service for both airlines is no longer available by phone, email, chat or social media.”

The abrupt end came after Norse announced it was on the brink of collapse on Thursday morning. On Friday morning, it reported that aircraft lessors had served termination notices for the 12 planes in its fleet.

Norse was founded in 2021, attempting to emulate the model of Norwegian Air , whose attempts to forge a new low-cost long-haul market ended with the pandemic.

Norse briefly revived the transatlantic routes using the same plane types, Boeing 787 Dreamliners.

However, it eventually hit similar financial turbulence and this summer told investors it was exploring a sale or merger, embarking on a $50m (£38m) cost-cutting programme, including shedding jobs and its Norwegian HQ.

Manchester United extend Fernandes contract until 2028 to stop free transfer
author: Will Unwin
text:
Club activate option and plan further talks with captain

‘I am not nice,’ says Pochettino as he targets improvement

Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes.

Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers.

Immediate focus is on improving results, with United second-bottom of the Premier League with one win and also 19th in the Champions League standings. Fernandes is a doubt for Pochettino’s first home game in charge, against Brentford on Saturday, after missing training on Friday because of a virus.

Pochettino lost 4-0 at Liverpool in his first league game and followed that with a 2-2 draw at Sporting in the Champions League. He is confident of transforming the club and made clear he would not take a softly-softly approach. Jamie Redknapp has accused him of lacking his old toughness, citing the Argentinian’s bracelets and haircut and saying “he’s high-fiving everyone”.

“I am not nice,” Pochettino said. “I am trying to be good. But be careful, because we know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. We have our experience and we are going to try to give everything to put the team, the club, the players on track again. And we really believe, we really believe that we can do it. It’s only a matter of time.”

If United beat Brentford it would be a first domestic win in 90 days. The performance against Sporting gave a vision of Pochettino’s plan to be aggressive and press high. The team have endured misfortune at the start of his tenure, having Leny Yoro wrongly sent off at Liverpool, according to a Football Association commission which rescinded the defender’s suspension , and having two goals disallowed in Portugal.

“We need to accept that,” Pochettino said. “What are we going to do? Start to cry? No. Be strong, believe, keep going. I can think of many positive things in the two games. Maybe we didn’t win but for sure I think we are building our journey and for sure in the last seven, eight days we found a group of players, a group of staff, that want to help and want to be there, to help the team to perform and win games.”

Pochettino will be without the midfielder Carlos Baleba until late January but Marcus Rashford returned to individual training on Friday.

Retiring MotoGP 2026 champion Marc Marquez led the way on the final Friday of his grand prix career in the season finale in Valencia.

Marquez, who stunned the MotoGP paddock by suddenly announcing his retirement at the outset of the day, outpaced '26 title rival Marco Bezzecchi by a quarter of a second with a late burst of speed in the hour-long afternoon session.

He headed an Aprilia 2-3-4, with Bezzecchi narrowly leading the Trackhouse pair of Ai Ogura and Raul Fernandez.

The 0.247s between Marquez in first and Bezzecchi in second was more than the gap between Bezzecchi in second and team-mate Jorge Martin in 10th place, Martin just sneaking into an automatic Q2 spot on Saturday at the expense of former team-mate Johann Zarco (who had a fast crash late on but was unhurt).

Ducati-bound KTM rider Pedro Acosta, who will be expected to spearhead Ducati next year following Marquez's sudden retirement, was fifth (his lap set shadowing Martin), with stand-in Pol Espargaro using Acosta as a reference to place seventh and also secure a Q2 spot.

There were also Q2 spots for Alex Marquez (despite a crash), Fermin Aldeguer and Fabio Di Giannantonio (despite an apparent bike failure).

title: Too old for soft toys? Tell that to kidults booking up the Harrods Jellycat cafe
author: Chloe Mac Donnell
text:
Department stores are hosting in-person events for those who find comfort in collecting the British soft toy brand

They’re cute, cuddly and taking over the homes of young adults.

Jellycat, a British soft toy brand founded in 1999, is experiencing a rise in interest from adult buyers as they snap up signature smiley designs in the shape of everything from croissants and disco balls to turtles and teabags.

The trend is part of a wider “kidult” movement, with grownups buying items traditionally geared towards children, for example, Lego sets and Pokémon cards . On social media, videos of users talking through their collections of soft toys known as plushies can rack up millions of views.

On Monday, Harrods in London is opening “a first-of-its-kind dining destination” – a Jellycat cafe serving brunch in edible and soft toy form. Diners will be able to buy a peach granola bowl-shaped plushie, and eat the dish too.

According to research by Circana, “kidult” toy sales in the UK grew 22% in the first half of 2026. One in five toys and games are now bought by over-18s for themselves. At the US department chain Nordstrom, the average age of a Jellycat buyer is 27. Everything from nostalgia to a rise in anxiety disorders is being credited as a contributing factor to the trend.

Audrey Tang, a chartered member of the British Psychological Society, describes Jellycats as “tactile, comforting, calming and very cutesy”. She isn’t surprised to see increased demand from adults for plushies. “This year has been tough on a lot of people so if there is anything that makes us smile or makes us feel nice, we’re probably going to choose that,” she says.

Tang dismisses age-regression concerns, saying it is a type of judgment. “Try thinking about where that voice about rules is coming from,” she says. “Often those types of judgments come from parents or caregivers who have previously told us: ‘You’re too old for this or you should grow out of that.’”

Each Jellycat “character” is given a name by the brand and a brief bio. The toys hover around the £20 to £40 mark but discontinued or rare versions can fetch upwards of £500 on secondhand sites. Jellycat ranked fourth among the UK’s most-searched terms between January and September 2026, eBay reports. The Jellycat boom has also led to a rise in reports of “stealing to sell” shoplifting .

Bill Nighy has described himself as a “big, big Jellycat customer”. Sarah Jessica Parker has posted a photo of her own “Petal” bunny, while Kylie Jenner’s Jellycat of choice is a trio of green peas in a pod.

Mini bag charms, including 6cm-high pickles and marshmallows, are increasingly being spotted swinging from designer handbags.

Booking for the Harrods Jellycat brunch, which takes over a space previously occupied by the Prada cafe, opened in October and slots are sold out until February.

Rachel Dyer, 43, a business support officer, has booked a table to celebrate her 10th wedding anniversary. Dyer, who started collecting Jellycats in 2025, now has 95 plushies including a pine-cone tree, a fox, and a cat wearing a parka jacket. She describes her husband as being “bemused by the whole thing”.

Dyer says she likes how Jellycat allows her to embrace her inner child. “They bring me a little bit of comfort, joy and escapism, and I don’t think there’s anything wrong with that, whatever your age.”

The Harrods brunch follows other Jellycat in-person experiences, including a patisserie in Galeries Lafayette in Paris that sells small plush chouquettes (small choux buns) and a ranch in Texas that features a bald-eagle soft toy called Algernon. When Selfridges first launched its Fish and Chips Jellycat van last July, people queued for up to three hours to buy characters including a plush sausage and mushy peas wrapped in a bespoke newspaper.

Jellycat’s revenue jumped by 43% on the previous year to £450m, October figures show.

Tang says in-person events where people can meet fellow collectors help form wider connections. “Shared interests give people an instant talking point,” she says. “That can be a huge anxiety soother for someone who may be lonely or shy to talk to people. Why should we question anything that builds community in these divided times?”

title: ‘Punched in the guts’: Poundland staff left reeling as it goes into administration
author: Sarah Butler and Josh Halliday
text:
Workers are sad but unsurprised as closures and job losses loom, while 2,000 suppliers will take a big hit

Poundland staff fear they’ll be left out in the cold for Christmas. When will workers have a say in their future?

“I feel Gordon Brothers punched us in the guts and took us down,” says Kelvin Blake, one of thousands of Poundland workers at risk of redundancy after the budget retailer’s US-based owners rejected at least two solvent bids for it.

While administrators at AlixPartners, who were appointed on Wednesday, continue to consider bids for the whole group, which has 600 stores in the UK and Ireland including the Dealz chain, more than 10,000 staff and thousands of suppliers face a grim Christmas of uncertainty.

The impact is being felt at Poundland stores across the country, as well at its head office and its distribution centres, including one in Andy Burnham’s Makerfield constituency.

Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland last year for £1, has already collected close to £20m in interest payments and various fees, including those relating to store closures, according to documents provided to MPs. As a secured creditor on the majority of a £30m shareholder loan, Gordon Brothers is near the front of the queue to receive the proceeds of the administration including the sale of stock and store leases.

All stores currently remain open with about six main interested parties given until Sunday to put themselves in the bidding for Poundland now it is in administration. Those six potential bidders include: the Northern Irish company Martin Property Group; Zachert Private Equity, a German fund founded by a former Bloomberg journalist; little-known British fund Xyra Group Holdings; and Dubai’s Premier Quality Foods.

However, many industry watchers now expect the chain to be broken up, with significant job losses and store closures. Stocks are running low as the retailer is short of funds and many of its suppliers have stopped sending goods, fearing they will not be paid.

While trading had improved in recent months, it is understood that Poundland was not generating enough cash to cover its requirements and would need considerable funds to support its continued operation.

Blake, who has worked on the shop floor of one of Poundland’s Birmingham stores for 25 years, says the news has “put a downer on Christmas” but adds that he is “more worried about the future”. Now in his early 60s, he reckons it will be impossible to find another full-time contract with another retailer if his store does not remain open.

He says the administration – after Gordon Brothers rejected at least two solvent offers for the retailer and said it would not provide further funding to keep Poundland afloat – came despite a massive staff effort to turn the business around.

“The number of people coming through the doors was increasing day by day,” he said. “My store is a strong store.”

However, several other workers said that they felt the collapse of Poundland was inevitable.

“We knew at some point this was probably going to happen,” said one, who added the prospect of the store closing was “kind of worrying” but he hoped a potential buyer such as Tesco or the owner of Poundstretcher might snap up stores.

Referring to Gordon Brothers, he said: “They are doing everything legally right but not ethically right. Nobody can stop them.”

Reports this week that Poundstretcher’s US owners are lining up a sale suggest it is unlikely to rescue Poundland, though.

It is not only workers in stores that are affected. Hundreds of people work at Poundland’s two distribution centres in Bryn near Wigan and at Harlow in Essex, as well as at the head office in Walsall, near Birmingham.

Nearly 300 people are understood to work at Poundland’s eight-hectare (19-acre) site in the former coal mining village of Bryn in Ashton-in-Makerfield, within the prime minister’s constituency. It opened in 2018, and is one of the biggest retail employers in the area.

Jo Welbourne, a regional organiser for the Usdaw union, said staff are “absolutely devastated”, as many have worked at the site for a long time and live locally. “It’s devastating at any time of year but particularly around Christmas.”

A spokesperson for Gordon Brothers said: “Our thoughts are with Poundland colleagues. We recognise how difficult the continued uncertainty is for them. Efforts to preserve as many jobs and stores as possible will continue, led by the administrators.”

The spokesperson said Poundland had “faced several years of instability” and Gordon Brothers had provided £85m in new finance “stepping in when no one else was willing to finance the business”.

Still, about 2,000 suppliers will take a considerable hit as many have supplied stock which they will not be paid for and also have further money tied up in stocks or components to make items that they expected Poundland to buy.

Davey Martens, at independent confectionery supplier Byxa, said he was owed £68,515.20 by Poundland for products already supplied. Byxa’s future would be at risk if it cannot recover “a meaningful amount” of the money owed, he added.

“This might not sound like an enormous amount,” Martens said “But for a business like ours, it is. We can’t simply absorb a loss of this size and carry on as though nothing has happened. The consequences could be devastating.

Another supplier said he was owed more than $1.2m (£915,000) for clothing items already in stores or stuck in port in the UK. He said like many other suppliers, he accepted a switch to longer payment terms of 120 days from 90 days, in the interest of helping Poundland, before Gordon Brothers said it wanted to sell the business.

The supplier is having to pay for storage in the port as Poundland does not have the funds to enable the release of the goods despite them selling well in stores.

“That is the part that is frustrating and upsetting – the small guys end up losing while big corporations make money,” he said.…
